fix(ioutils): propagate ContainerError.Kind to ExecutionError.Recoverability in ReadError

`RemoteFileOutputReader.ReadError` reads the container's `error.pb` and
already sets the Go-level `io.ExecutionError.IsRecoverable` bool from
`ContainerError.Kind`. It does not, however, populate the proto-level
`core.ExecutionError.Recoverability` field on the wrapped
`*core.ExecutionError`. The proto-level field is what downstream services
see when the `ExecutionError` is serialized across the wire (the
in-process Go bool is dropped during proto encoding), so they currently
observe the proto3 zero value (`NON_RECOVERABLE`) for every error
regardless of intent.

Set `Recoverability` from `errorDoc.Error.Kind` so the bit makes it onto
the wire intact. The Go-level `IsRecoverable` continues to be set in
parallel for in-process callers; both agree.

Without this, a `NonRecoverableError` raised by user task code is
indistinguishable on the wire from a recoverable failure, defeating the
contract that NonRecoverableError consumes no retries.

Upgrade to go-grpc-middleware/providers/prometheus (#686)

## Overview
The deprecated grpc prometheus metrics [do not handle native errors](https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/go-grpc-prometheus/blob/master/packages/grpcstatus/grpcstatus.go#L37-L57) like Canceled or DeadlineExceeded and instead surface these as Unknown errors. The [latest grpc middleware](https://github.com/grpc-ecosystem/go-grpc-middleware/blob/509959fc2702e89b40541afeb65e561854e1f545/providers/prometheus/options.go#L18) on the other hand does adds proper grpc_code labels for these context error types.

This change replaces the old grpc prometheus metric provider with the new one and wires up to existing services and clients. Note, the new metrics provider doesn't have a global default, which makes wiring up multiple clients or single binary somewhat difficult. To resolve this, `grpcutils` was added to init default client and server grpc metric providers.

## Test Plan
- [x] Run single binary and verify grpc metrics are available
- [x] Bring to cloud and verify integration works as expected

fix(connector): guard ClientSet with a mutex and tidy client accessors

Address review feedback:
- ClientSet maps are accessed from the connector poll loop and from concurrent
  task handlers; guard all access with a ClientSet mutex via getOrDial* /
  metadataClient helpers. This also closes a pre-existing race on
  asyncConnectorClients (getAsyncConnectorClient wrote it unlocked from
  concurrent Create/Get/Delete).
- getConnectorMetadataClient returned only an error despite being named/doc'd
  like it returns a cached client; replaced with cs.getOrDialMetadataClient
  which returns (client, error), consistent with the async path.
- Test: use a cancelable context so the dial-close goroutine is cleaned up, and
  a passthrough:/// target so no DNS/network is attempted.

Verified with go test -race.

fix(flyte-devbox): use relative redirect for console root route

The root-to-console redirectRegex echoed back the scheme+host captured
from the request URL. Behind proxies that rewrite Host (e.g. GitHub
Codespaces forwarded addresses), Traefik sees http://localhost:30080/
and the browser is redirected there instead of the public URL.

Replace the whole matched URL with just the console base path so the
browser receives a relative redirect (Location: /v2) and resolves it
against the URL it actually requested. Works equally for direct access
and any proxy in front of the devbox.

add INITIALIZING state to actor environment management (#623)

## Overview
Currently, if all of the `createPods` calls fail when creating an environment, the environment is still maintained in the in-memory store. This allows other tasks to request and retrieve it (updating the TTL expiration). However, the other tasks will be stuck in a "no workers available" state indefinitely (because creating the replica Pods fails). The result, is that when two (or more) tasks execute in relative unison, if the replica Pod creation will never succeed (ex. incorrect volume mount) there is the _potential_ that the system gets stuck continually attempting to create replica Pods rather than fast failing.

This PR introduces an INITIALIZING state to ensure cleanup of environments if creating initial pods fails.

## Test Plan
This was tested locally.

## Rollout Plan (if applicable)
May be rolled out immediately.

* feat(storage): multi-scheme DataStore with lazy per-scheme backend routing

Replace the single-purpose redis scheme-routing store with a general
routing store. The configured Type is built eagerly as the primary
backend (owning the InitContainer and GetBaseContainerFQN); every other
scheme (s3://, gs://, abfs://, redis://, ...) is dialed lazily on first
reference and memoized for reuse, so one DataStore can serve any
scheme/container. Schemes absent from the optional per-scheme config map
are dialed with ambient credentials. Cross-scheme CopyRaw routes through
the store itself.

[BUG] array node eventing bump version (#5680)

* [BUG] add retries to handle array node eventing race condition (#421)

If there is an error updating a [FlyteWorkflow CRD](https://github.com/unionai/flyte/blob/6a7207c5345604a28a9d4e3699becff767f520f5/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/handler.go#L378), then the propeller streak ends without the CRD getting updated and the in-memory copy of the FlyteWorkflow is not utilized on the next loop.

[TaskPhaseVersion](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/apis/flyteworkflow/v1alpha1/node_status.go#L239) is stored in the FlyteWorkflow. This is incremented when there is an update to node/subnode state to ensure that events are unique. If the events stay in the same state and have the same TaskPhaseVersion, then they [get short-circuited and don't get emitted to admin](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/events/admin_eventsink.go#L59) or will get returned as an [AlreadyExists error](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flyteadmin/pkg/manager/impl/task_execution_manager.go#L172) and get [handled in propeller to not bubble up in an error](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/nodes/node_exec_context.go#L38).

We can run into issues with ArrayNode eventing when:
- array node handler increments task phase version from "0" to "1"
- admin event sink emits event with version "1"
- the propeller controller is not able to update the FlyteWorkflow CRD, so the ArrayNodeStatus indicates taskPhaseVersion is still 0
- next loop, array node handler increments task phase version from "0" to "1"
- admin event sink prevents the event from getting emitted as an event with the same ID has already been received. No error is bubbled up.

This means we lose subnode state until there is an event that contains an update to that subnode. If the lost state is the subnode reaching a terminal state, then the subnode state (from admin/UI) is "stuck" in a non-terminal state.

I confirmed this to be an issue in the load-test-cluster. Whenever, there was an [error syncing the FlyteWorkflow](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/workers.go#L91), the next round of eventing in ArrayNode would fail unless the ArrayNode phase changed.

BugFix: Timeout should cause the existing execution to abort and these should be finite (#71)

Bug 1; Execution Timeout currently has a bug such that the existing execution is not aborted. Thus the execution continues to run in the background potentially consuming resources.

Bug 2; On a task timeout the UI shows the existing task as running and a new execution begins

Bug 3; Timeouts could cause infinite retries, as it bypassed the retry logic

Solution
Every timeout is treated like a retryable failure, and every retryable failure enforces an abort to be invoked. Abort was already expected to be idempotent, thus invoking it for a terminated execution should not cause side-effects

+improvements
Finalize Child workflow always, even if finalizing parent fails

whose last observation moves with every repeat, so an event describes an interval
and not a moment: first recorded at one time, still firing at another. Relevance
was decided on the last observation alone, which discarded the case that matters
most. Hardware that goes on faulting after the container died has a last
observation well past the failure, so a fault created a minute before the pod
died but still firing eleven minutes later was rejected for being two minutes too
late, and the longer the hardware kept faulting the more certainly its fault was
thrown away.

Deciding on the creation alone would break the opposite case, which the previous
behaviour got right: a fault first recorded before the window opened but still
firing when the task died is exactly the fault that killed it.

faultOverlapsFailure keeps both. The event is active over the stretch from when
it was first recorded to when it was last seen, the failure is relevant over the
window before it and the small slack after it, and the fault counts when those
two stretches overlap. A fault that only started after the failure is still
rejected, and so is one that had stopped firing before the window opened.

The slack's meaning is narrowed to match: it bounds when a fault started, not
when it stopped, because how long dying hardware goes on faulting says nothing
about whether it caused the failure.

Treat K8s Invalid/BadRequest on resource create as permanent user failure

K8s rejects a deterministically invalid resource (e.g. a pod spec with an
empty container image) with 422 on every create attempt. launchResource
previously fell through to the generic system-error path, so leasor
system-retried up to max_system_retries (30) at ~1/min, flipping the
action back to Queued while the previous attempt's error stayed on the
record — the "Queued but error" UI state.

Handle IsInvalid and IsBadRequest like EntityTooLarge: a permanent user
failure that fails the action immediately.

* Use bet version of ingress (#988)

"Hey so, I noticed that you are using the Ingress class out of beta, which is kind of an issue-- the Ingress class was moved out of beta in the 1.19 release, which happened in late august. If flyte is run in clusters older than this (e.g. 1.18), then this will fail. EKS only started offering 1.19 a couple of months ago, and the GKE regular channel defaults to 1.18, so this really won't work for most of your users. Do you guys mind if I file a pr to move back to the beta ingress version? I don't see you guys using anyhting required from the GA version, and beta has been serving everyone well for the past 6 years"

feat(idl): add TaskTemplate.worker_kind (#8134)

The kind of worker that runs a task, as an enum. The scheduler sends a
task only to workers of its kind and holds it while none has room;
unspecified is the default worker that runs containers and plugin tasks.
WORKER_KIND_SANDBOX runs flyte.sandbox.orchestrator source in an
interpreter, with no container.

Routing on the task type string alone cannot tell a type the default
worker runs from one only a specialised worker can run, so it depended on
which workers were connected: when the specialised worker restarted, its
tasks went to the default worker and failed.

fix(propeller): record events Admin already has in the dedup filter (#7852)

The event sink only adds an event id to its dedup filter after a clean send.
When Admin answers AlreadyExists, the id is never recorded, so every re-emit of
that event passes the filter, takes a token from the sink's rate limiter and
makes a round trip that cannot succeed.

An execution that keeps re-emitting a recorded event can exhaust the limiter and
starve the other executions sharing it.

Record the id when Admin reports it already has the event, or that the entity is
already terminal. The error is still returned, so callers see what they saw
before.

feat(flytek8s): request per-partition accelerator resources for MIG mixed strategy (#8165)

## Why are the changes needed?

Under the NVIDIA device plugin's mixed MIG strategy, a node doesn't offer its MIG slices as `nvidia.com/gpu`. Each profile is its own resource, `nvidia.com/mig-<profile>` (for example `nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb`). Today a task that asks for a partition always requests the device class's base resource and gets a partition-size node affinity, which only works with the single strategy, so there's no way to schedule a partitioned task on a mixed-strategy cluster.

## What changes were proposed in this pull request?

`AcceleratorDeviceClassConfig` gains an optional `partition-resource-name` template. Every `{partition}` in it is replaced with the task's partition size, so `nvidia.com/mig-{partition}` turns a 1g.5gb partition into a request for `nvidia.com/mig-1g.5gb`.

With the template set, a task with a partition:

- requests the rendered resource in place of the device class's resource name, with the same count
- keeps the base resource's tolerations, since partitioned nodes are tainted like any other node of that class
- keeps the base resource's platform limits, and a platform limit set for the partition resource itself wins
- drops the partition-size node affinity and toleration, because only nodes that offer that profile can satisfy the resource

Unpartitioned requests still use the base resource name, and configs without the template behave exactly as before.

## How was this patch tested?

New unit tests in `flytek8s` cover rendering and matching partition resource names, mapping them back to the device class, tolerations, resource overrides and limits, GPU sanitizing, and pod specs with and without the template (partitioned, whole GPU, and explicitly unpartitioned). `go test ./go/tasks/pluginmachinery/flytek8s/...` passes in `flyteplugins`.

fix(devbox): read the kubeconfig from the container in `make start`

`make devbox-run` fails against an already-running devbox that was started
with a different host dir at /.kube:

    Waiting for kubeconfig...
    chown: cannot access '/.kube/kubeconfig': No such file or directory

The target waited on $(PWD)/.kube/kubeconfig and then chown'd /.kube/kubeconfig
inside the container, assuming both are the same bind mount. When they are not,
a stale host file satisfies the wait instantly and the exec then fails — the
guard checks a path that cannot report the problem it is guarding against.

Read the kubeconfig out of the container instead. That is correct however the
devbox was started, and a stale host file can no longer pass the wait. It also
drops the chown: the shell redirect writes the file as the invoking user, which
is what that WSL workaround existed to achieve.

Signed-off-by: Kevin Su <pingsutw@apache.org>

docs(monitoring): explain the grafana_dashboard label value

"Why 1?" is a fair question, and the answer is not "convention" as it is with
some sidecars. kube-prometheus-stack sets LABEL_VALUE=1 on the dashboard
sidecar, so it matches the key *and* the value — a ConfigMap labelled
grafana_dashboard: "true" is silently ignored. Only when LABEL_VALUE is empty
does any value match.

Documents how to read both env vars off the running sidecar, so people check
their own deployment instead of copying a value that worked elsewhere and
wondering why nothing appears.

Also notes the quotes are required: label values are strings, and unquoted 1 is
a YAML integer that kubectl rejects with "cannot unmarshal number into Go struct
field ObjectMeta.metadata.labels of type string".

feat(runs): merge userinfo into missing identity fields, not all-or-nothing

Previously the enricher skipped userinfo whenever the headers already supplied any
profile field, so the cookie path kept its email but never gained a name, and the
Bearer path got a name but no email. Now it fetches userinfo whenever the profile is
incomplete and fills only the missing fields, keeping header-provided values
authoritative. Claims are cached per subject (raw), so a partial profile still costs
at most one userinfo call per subject per TTL. Result: full name + email on both
paths, subject to the token's granted scopes.

fix(copilot): download multipart blob items through the authenticated store

Stow's S3 backend reports listed items as public
https://s3-<region>.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/<key> URLs, so StowStore.List
hands copilot http(s) references for every file in a directory input.
handleBlob then fetched each one with an unauthenticated
http.DefaultClient GET, which a private bucket answers with 403
AccessDenied. DownloadFileFromHTTP never checked the status code, so the
XML error body was written to disk as the file's content and counted as
a successful download: every Dir input to a raw-container/shell task on
S3 arrived as a directory of identical ~263-byte error documents.

Read each item back through the DataStore under the blob's own scheme
(rebuilding <blob uri>/<relative path> when List returned an http(s)
URL); only blobs whose URI is itself http(s) are fetched over HTTP. Also
make DownloadFileFromHTTP fail on non-2xx responses so an error page can
never again be staged as data.

feat(flyteidl2): ArtifactService.ListArtifactMetadataKeys

Add an RPC that returns the distinct user_metadata keys seen on recently
created artifacts in a project (keys only, never values), so the console's
artifact filters can suggest keys instead of requiring them to be typed.

The response is sorted and capped server-side and may be served from a
short-lived cache; keys present only on artifacts outside the server's
recency window may be absent, so clients keep accepting free-text keys.

Scoop update for flytestdlib version v0.2.5

feat(runs): implement IdentityService.UserInfo from forwarded auth headers

UserInfo was a stub returning an empty UserInfoResponse, so `flyte whoami`
printed an empty record for every caller.

Resolve the caller through the same path run attribution already uses —
identityFromHeaders over the configured proxy-forwarded headers, then the OIDC
userinfo enricher on the Bearer path — so whoami and a run's executed_by can
never disagree about who someone is. Reuses the existing helpers rather than
adding a second identity code path.

Returns Unauthenticated when the request carries no identity, or when
trustForwardedIdentityHeaders is off (the caller cannot be established at all),
so whoami reports not-logged-in instead of printing an empty record.

fix(ray): apply interruptible scheduling to Ray head and worker pods

Ray head/worker pod templates re-applied GPU node selectors after the
custom k8s_pod merge but never re-applied interruptible scheduling. The
merge (mergo WithAppendSlice) appends a custom pod's node selector terms
as new OR'd terms, so the (Non)InterruptibleNodeSelectorRequirement
seeded by ToK8sPodSpec only landed on the base term. A non-interruptible
task whose worker carried its own affinity could therefore still be
scheduled onto a spot node.

Add an idempotent flytek8s.ApplyInterruptibleScheduling helper that
re-applies the (non)interruptible node-affinity requirement to every
node selector term plus the interruptible node selector and tolerations,
and call it post-merge in buildHeadPodTemplate / buildWorkerPodTemplate
(mirroring the existing GPU re-apply). Head and worker both follow the
task's interruptible flag.

Adds TestBuildResourceRayInterruptible (head + worker, both flag values,
with exactly-once idempotency assertions) and the OR-hole regression
TestBuildResourceRayInterruptibleCustomAffinity.

fix(actions): record actions on ADDED always, other events only with dedup filter

Preserve the original watch event type through the coalesced path instead of
hardcoding Modified: an object's first event is always ADDED and can never be
coalesced away (its marker cannot pre-exist), so ADDED survives to gate
RecordAction. notifyRunService then records on ADDED unconditionally, and on
other non-delete events only when the dedup filter is configured — so an
explicitly disabled filter (recordFilterSize<=0) degrades to the pre-existing
record-on-ADDED behavior instead of issuing RecordAction (and parent
promotion) RPCs on every watch update.

fix: derive KService name from a namespace digest and a literal app name

Move the app name out of the hashed identity: the digest now covers only
org, project and domain, and the name is carried literally as
k-{name}-{digest}.

This keeps INTERNAL_APP_ENDPOINT_PATTERN working. The pattern is a constant
template with a single {app_fqdn} slot that app code fills with a target's
name, so it can only survive if everything else in the KService name is
constant across the namespace. Hashing the name made that impossible; hashing
only the namespace makes the digest shared by every app a pod can address, so
it is resolved at deploy time and baked into the value.

Because the name is no longer hashed, the literal segment has to be injective
by itself — a truncation or a trimmed hyphen would merge two apps onto one
KService, which is the bug this scheme exists to prevent. KServiceName now
returns an error for a name it cannot represent rather than reshaping it.
Everything the proto admits is representable, so this only fires on an
identity that reached us without validation.

App names are case-insensitive, so the name segment is lowercased; project
and domain are not, and are hashed as given.

NamespacedNameSuffixTemplate is removed: the endpoint pattern no longer
reproduces the KService name by string template, so the config had no effect.

SignalEvent gives UI/CLI a run-scoped endpoint to resolve a paused condition
action. It carries the condition's ActionIdentifier, the owning
parent_action_name (for actions-service shard routing), and the user-facing
typed EventPayload (bool/int/float/string oneof). Backends that route to a
dedicated actions service convert the payload to a core.Literal and delegate
to ActionsService.Signal; the single-binary backend returns Unimplemented.

single-binary RunService so it still satisfies RunServiceHandler.

Retry a Ray job KubeRay lost track of

KubeRay sets JobDeploymentStatusFailed with reason
JobDeploymentStatusTransitionGracePeriodExceeded when the RayJob's status
never transitioned within the grace period. The job's outcome is unknown and
the task's code may never have run, so no error file is written. The plugin
mapped that to a terminal user failure, permanently killing the task without
consuming a retry.

Map that one reason to a retryable system failure with cleanup, so the retry
gets a fresh Ray cluster. Every other failure reason, including AppFailed,
keeps its existing behaviour and the RECOVERABLE error.pb path is unchanged.

fix(propeller/k8s): treat BadRequest / Invalid from apiserver as permanent failure (#7366)

* fix(propeller): treat K8s BadRequest/Invalid errors as permanent failures

When creating a task pod fails with a BadRequest (HTTP 400) or Invalid
(HTTP 422) error from the K8s API server, propeller currently falls
through to the default branch and surfaces it as a retryable system
error. The user's workflow then burns through its retry budget making
the same request that will never succeed.

These errors are intrinsic to the request payload — most commonly a
validating admission webhook rejecting the pod spec, or an invalid
field value caught by the apiserver. Retrying with the same input
produces the same rejection.

The fix path was already written but commented out since #1 (2019) with
no documented rationale; uncomment it so BadRequest / Invalid produce
a permanent failure with code "BadTaskFormat", matching how the
neighboring EntityTooLarge case is already handled.

Closes #6531

fix(plugins): classify CreateContainerError as system-retryable instead of user error

When a pod fails with CreateContainerError or CreateContainerConfigError
and the grace period is exceeded, the error was classified as a USER
permanent failure. This prevented system retries from triggering, causing
tasks to fail immediately even when retries were configured.

These errors are typically transient infrastructure issues (e.g. "failed
to reserve container name") that should be retried by the system. Changed
both error paths to use PhaseInfoSystemRetryableFailureWithCleanup so
that max-node-retries-system-failures can handle them.

Closes #6786

Add FLYTE_DISABLE_TELEMETRY opt-out and telemetry.enabled chart value

FLYTE_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true is now the one switch shared by flyte-sdk,
the backend and the console. A new flytestdlib/telemetry package owns the
check (DO_NOT_TRACK and the legacy FLYTE_DISABLE_SENTRY are honoured too)
and sentryutils uses it.

A backend with telemetry disabled passes FLYTE_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true on to
the task pods and apps it creates, so the SDK inside them stays quiet without
any per-task configuration. It is appended last, so a task's own env cannot
undo the deployment's opt-out.

The flyte-binary and flyte-core charts gain telemetry.enabled (default true).
Setting it to false sets the variable on every backend component and the
console; the devbox dev-mode console follows flyte-binary.telemetry.enabled.

feat(executor): fall back to non-interruptible capacity on the last attempt

Interruptible tasks ran on interruptible capacity for every attempt, so a
task whose nodes kept being reclaimed could burn its whole retry budget
without ever landing on capacity that survives.

The new executor `interruptibleFailureThreshold` sets the attempt count at
which a task falls back to non-interruptible capacity. It defaults to -1,
which moves only the final attempt; a value above the maximum disables the
fallback, and zero is rejected at startup. Either the task's own retries or
the system-failure budget can trip it, and at least one attempt always runs
on interruptible capacity.

fix(copilot): download multipart blob items through the authenticated store (#8077)

Stow's S3 backend reports listed items as public
https://s3-<region>.amazonaws.com/<bucket>/<key> URLs, so StowStore.List
hands copilot http(s) references for every file in a directory input.
handleBlob then fetched each one with an unauthenticated
http.DefaultClient GET, which a private bucket answers with 403
AccessDenied. DownloadFileFromHTTP never checked the status code, so the
XML error body was written to disk as the file's content and counted as
a successful download: every Dir input to a raw-container/shell task on
S3 arrived as a directory of identical ~263-byte error documents.

Read each item back through the DataStore under the blob's own scheme
(rebuilding <blob uri>/<relative path> when List returned an http(s)
URL); only blobs whose URI is itself http(s) are fetched over HTTP. Also
make DownloadFileFromHTTP fail on non-2xx responses so an error page can
never again be staged as data.

window without raising maxReservationHeartbeat too still leaves a gap.

fix: make devbox build work with Helm v4

`make devbox-build` runs `kustomize build --enable-helm`, and kustomize
< v5.8.0 probes Helm with `helm version -c --short`. Helm v4 removed the
`-c` shorthand, so the build fails for any developer who has Helm v4
installed:

    Error: unknown shorthand flag: 'c' in -c
    : unable to run: 'helm version -c --short' ...

Pin kustomize to v5.8.1 (adds Helm v4 support via kustomize#6016 and
fixes the v5.8.0 namespace-propagation regression via kustomize#6044),
and have the devbox manifests target use the executor's pinned kustomize
binary instead of whatever kustomize the developer happens to have on
PATH, so the build is reproducible regardless of local helm/kustomize.

fix: Add deterministic error clearing for FAIL_AFTER_EXECUTABLE_NODES_COMPLETE

This commit addresses the determinism concern raised in PR #4624 by ensuring
that error clearing behavior is consistent across reconciliation rounds.

The issue: When multiple nodes fail with FAIL_AFTER_EXECUTABLE_NODES_COMPLETE
policy, only one error should be preserved to reduce etcd state size. However,
the previous implementation could clear ALL errors if iteration order varied
between reconciliation rounds.

The fix: Before clearing an error from a node status, check if the error is
still present (not nil). Once an error is cleared, that node won't be
considered as a "new" failure in subsequent rounds, ensuring determinism
regardless of map iteration order.

Changes:
- Add ClearExecutionError() method to MutableNodeStatus interface
- Implement ClearExecutionError() in NodeStatus struct
- Add nil check in handleDownstream before error clearing
- Add comprehensive unit tests for the new behavior

fix(executor): honor task-level interruptible when the run-level flag is unset

The executor read interruptibility only from TaskAction.Spec.Interruptible,
which is populated from the run-level RunSpec. Interruptible set at the
TaskEnvironment, @env.task, or task.override() level serializes into the
embedded TaskTemplate metadata but never reached pod scheduling, so the
plugins.k8s interruptible node affinity and tolerations were not applied.

The task template's metadata now decides interruptibility whenever the
run-level flag is unset; an explicit run-level value still wins.

fix(copilot): stage set Optional[File] inputs like File under NAMED_DIR (#8118)

Under the NAMED_DIR layout a single File input is staged inside a
per-input directory under its original basename (/var/inputs/<var>/<name>),
which is what shell tasks glob for (/var/inputs/<var>/*). singleBlob only
recognised a bare blob literal, though, and an Optional[File] input is
serialized as a union wrapping the blob. So a set optional file fell
through to the plain path and was written as /var/inputs/<var> itself: the
glob matched nothing and the script silently behaved as if the input were
unset (e.g. STAR dropped mate 2 of a paired-end sample; salmon index
skipped its decoy genome).

Unwrap union literals in singleBlob so a set Optional[File] stages exactly
like a File. An unset optional (union of none) is unchanged and never
becomes a per-input directory.

artifact: parent is a full artifact reference, not a bare version

Replaces ArtifactSpec.parent_version and ProducedArtifact.parent_version
(same field numbers — the string fields shipped in v2.0.46 but nothing
consumes them yet, so a clean break beats a reserved graveyard) with
parent_artifact, a core.ArtifactVersionId.

A bare version string could only express lineage within one artifact
name. A full reference lets a version record derivation across
artifacts — a model deriving from a dataset version — while keeping the
common same-name case as terse as before: empty key fields inherit the
child's own scope and name, so {version: "v1"} still means "the v1 of
this same artifact".

The parent must live in the artifact's own org/project/domain (same
convention as ArtifactSource provenance). Everything else is unchanged:
stored as given, never resolved, dangling parents legal, immutable
after creation. The ListArtifacts children filter becomes the
parent_name + parent_version EQUAL pair, always together, replacing the
name-scoped parent_version filter.

Sort node IDs for deterministic workflow compilation

The ValidateWorkflow function iterates wf.Nodes (a Go map) in two
places without sorting keys. Since Go map iteration order is
randomized, the same workflow can produce different compiled outputs
across compilations. This causes FlyteAdmin's digest comparison to
fail for structurally identical workflows, triggering the
"different structure" code path with an oversized jsondiff error.

Sort node IDs before iterating to ensure deterministic edge
ordering in the CompiledWorkflowClosure. This makes identical
workflows produce identical digests, so re-registration correctly
returns ALREADY_EXISTS.

fix(gpufault): review fixes for classification trust, scope and shape

Four defects from code review of the classification path.

Events are now trusted by their reason, not their text: the executor only
parses events whose reason is the emitter's GPUXidError or GPUSXidError
(constants the gpufault package now exports), and FromEventMessage re-derives
severity from the local table instead of honoring the message tail, so free
text in an event cannot pose as a critical fault. The event search is bounded
by a ten-minute relevance window, so an old fault on a long-lived pod cannot
reclassify every later, unrelated failure.

ClassifyFailure keeps the failure's shape: a permanent failure stays
permanent (the fault reclassifies whose problem it is, not whether the task
can run), a specific plugin code such as OOMKilled is kept and only generic
codes give way to the fault's, cleanupOnFailure survives the rebuild (a new
WithCleanupOnFailure helper; WithVersion also no longer drops the flag), and
Recoverability is no longer copied across a verdict change.

The severity table now agrees with the code table: 140 (unrecovered ECC), 62
and 109 are critical.

fix(flyteplugins): don't charge a user retry for an unreadable termination status (#8095)

fix(flyteplugins): do not charge a user retry for an unreadable termination status

When a pod is torn down before its container finishes, the kubelet cannot reach
the container's log to read the termination message. It records the read failure
in Message and reports a fabricated exit code, in practice 2.

DemystifyFailure attributes failures by exit code, and 2 <= maxUserExitCode, so
the fabricated code was taken as the application's own answer. The failure was
classified USER and a retry was spent on a disruption the user did not cause,
contradicting the documented guarantee that platform-caused failures do not
consume the retries=N budget.

The damage is silent. The run often still succeeds, so nothing surfaces until a
genuine transient error arrives and finds the budget already empty. It is worst
on spot and preemptible fleets, where graceful pod deletion is routine.

An exit code the kubelet could not read is no longer used to assign blame. Such
a status now falls through to the existing UnknownError handling, which already
treats an indeterminate outcome as system-level. That direction is the
conservative one: charging the platform for a user error costs nothing visible,
while charging the user for a platform disruption empties a budget they planned
around.

The guard is narrow. A container that genuinely exits non-zero with a readable
termination message is untouched and stays attributed to the user, which the
second new test case pins.

This is distinct from the SIGKILL path in #8067, which covers exit codes 137 and
247; this path produces exit code 2 and never reaches those branches.

Related to #8067

Honour DO_NOT_TRACK as the telemetry opt-out; add telemetry.enabled chart value (#8175)

* Add FLYTE_DISABLE_TELEMETRY opt-out and telemetry.enabled chart value

FLYTE_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true is now the one switch shared by flyte-sdk,
the backend and the console. A new flytestdlib/telemetry package owns the
check (DO_NOT_TRACK and the legacy FLYTE_DISABLE_SENTRY are honoured too)
and sentryutils uses it.

A backend with telemetry disabled passes FLYTE_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true on to
the task pods and apps it creates, so the SDK inside them stays quiet without
any per-task configuration. It is appended last, so a task's own env cannot
undo the deployment's opt-out.

The flyte-binary and flyte-core charts gain telemetry.enabled (default true).
Setting it to false sets the variable on every backend component and the
console; the devbox dev-mode console follows flyte-binary.telemetry.enabled.

feat: add LocalRunService for reporting locally-orchestrated runs (#7737)

* feat: add LocalRunService for reporting locally-orchestrated runs

Adds flyteidl2.workflow.LocalRunService: clients that orchestrate actions
outside the platform (e.g. on a user's machine) register a run and report
action state, while the read/watch surface reuses RunService's request and
response messages so existing clients and UIs work with only a service swap.

Also adds the control-plane-direct dataproxy surface for local run data:
UploadMetadata (signed PUT URLs for inputs.pb/outputs.pb/report.html),
GetLocalActionData and CreateLocalDownloadLink, plus ArtifactType
INPUTS/OUTPUTS values and RunSource.RUN_SOURCE_LOCAL.

Signed-off-by: Haytham Abuelfutuh <haytham@union.ai>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add AbortRun to LocalRunService

Marks a local run and all its non-terminal actions ABORTED server-side.
The platform cannot stop the local orchestrator, so this is a bookkeeping
abort: subsequent reports against aborted actions are rejected, and
aborting an already-terminal run is acknowledged as a no-op. Reuses
RunService's AbortRunRequest/AbortRunResponse messages.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01VJa4n1pjJUBVQbjeWCZJyQ
Signed-off-by: Haytham Abuelfutuh <haytham@afutuh.com>

* Rework local-run data path onto existing dataproxy APIs

Local runs no longer get dedicated dataproxy RPCs. Uploads use
CreateUploadLocation and reads use GetActionData/CreateDownloadLink,
routed like every other data operation: the client asks
ClusterService.SelectCluster (new OPERATION_LOCAL_RUN_DATA) and the
server answers with a dataplane endpoint when the org's clusters are
directly reachable, or its own endpoint otherwise — in which case the
control plane serves the artifacts from its own storage.

Two small extensions to existing messages make this routable:
- SelectClusterResponse.cluster names the selected cluster so reporters
  can stamp it on the action attempt; reads later route by the recorded
  attempt cluster (empty = control-plane storage).
- GetActionDataRequest.run_source disambiguates resolution: run names
  are not unique across platform and local runs, so RUN_SOURCE_LOCAL
  resolves the action via LocalRunService.

Removes UploadMetadata, GetLocalActionData, CreateLocalDownloadLink and
their request messages, and the INPUTS/OUTPUTS artifact types that only
they used.

fix(connector): reuse persistent connections for ListConnectors polling

watchConnectors re-dialed a fresh gRPC connection to every connector
endpoint on each PollInterval and closed it at the end of the tick, so
every ListConnectors paid a full TCP+HTTP/2 handshake through the ingress
path on each poll.

Reuse the persistent connections already held on Plugin.cs (built once at
init with the plugin's long-lived context), dialing only newly-added
endpoints — matching how GetTask already reuses its cached
AsyncConnectorService client. Also add conservative client keepalive so a
dead/half-open transport is detected in seconds rather than via the OS TCP
timeout.

fix: drop RunIdentifier.name pattern so ingest paths accept pre-existing run names (#7838)

* fix: drop RunIdentifier.name pattern so ingest paths accept pre-existing run names

PR #7805 added DNS-1035 run-name enforcement in two places: a validateRunName
check at CreateRun (the only external ingress for user-supplied names) and a
buf.validate pattern on RunIdentifier.name. The proto pattern was intended as
documentation, but in deployments where protovalidate is wired it is enforced
on every message embedding RunIdentifier — including event reporting and
record/status replication. Runs created before the rule existed became
un-ingestable mid-run: their updates were rejected with InvalidArgument and
retried or dropped, leaving the runs looking stuck while pods kept executing.

Remove the pattern (back to min_len/max_len) and keep validateRunName as the
single enforcement point. New invalid names are still rejected at CreateRun;
identifiers on read/report paths accept whatever was already created.

* feat(workflow): add ActionsService proto for action state APIs (#6899)

* feat(workflow): add ActionsService proto for action state APIs

Introduce a new flyteidl2/workflow/actions_service.proto that defines an
ActionsService consolidating state and queue functionality for actions.
Add RPCs to update and retrieve action state (UpdateActionStatus,
GetActionState), plus EnqueueAction, AbortQueuedAction, and Watch to
support queuing and observation. Define request/response messages for
UpdateActionStatus and GetActionState, including validation rules and
fields for action identifiers, attempt number, status, and serialized
NodeStatus state.

This centralizes action state/queue operations into a single service
intended to replace parts of the existing StateService and QueueService,
simplifies APIs for workers, and provides at-least-once semantics for
state watches.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* feat(proto): validate action attempt is greater than zero and regen pb

- Add buf.validate rule to require attempt > 0 for action request and
  response in actions_service.proto. This enforces that action
  attempts start from 1 and prevents zero-valued attempts from being
  accepted.
- Regenerate Go protobuf bindings (actions_service.pb.go) to reflect the
  added validation annotations and updated descriptor bytes.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* feat(actions): rename ActionsService RPCs and messages

Rename several RPCs and corresponding request/response messages to
simplify the ActionsService API and provide clearer, shorter names.

- Rename EnqueueAction -> Enqueue for queueing new actions.
- Rename Watch -> WatchForUpdates to clarify streaming semantics.
- Rename UpdateActionStatus -> Update and its request/response types to
  UpdateRequest/UpdateResponse.
- Rename GetActionState -> GetLatestState and its request/response types
  to GetLatestStateRequest/GetLatestStateResponse.
- Rename AbortQueuedAction -> Abort while keeping the original abort
  request/response payload types.
- Update comments to match the new names and keep deprecation notes.

These changes make the service surface more concise and consistent,
improving readability and aligning RPC names with their intent.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* feat(actions): extract ActionsService and add action RPC msgs

Move ActionsService into a dedicated flyteidl2.workflow.actions package and
adjust Go package path accordingly. Replace fully-qualified RPC types with
local message names for Enqueue, WatchForUpdates, and Abort RPCs to simplify
imports and proto usage.

Introduce new request/response messages for Enqueue:
- EnqueueRequest with action_id, optional parent_action_name, run_spec,
  input/run output paths, group, subject and a required oneof spec for
  Task/Trace/Condition actions.
- EnqueueResponse as an empty ack.

Add WatchForUpdatesRequest/WatchForUpdatesResponse messages to support
streaming updates with filtering by parent_action_id and payloads that
carry either ActionUpdate or ControlMessage.

Minor changes:
- Import flyteidl2/task/run.proto for RunSpec.
- Add buf.validate annotations and field constraints for required fields.

These changes centralize action-related APIs, improve type locality in the
proto, and prepare the ActionsService to replace previous StateService and
QueueService behaviors.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* feat(generated): add gRPC ActionsService stubs and servicer

Add generated gRPC Python bindings for the ActionsService into the
workflow actions package. This creates ActionsServiceStub with unary and
streaming RPC methods (Enqueue, GetLatestState, WatchForUpdates,
Update, Abort) wired to the protobuf serializers/deserializers, and an
ActionsServiceServicer skeleton that returns UNIMPLEMENTED for each
method.

These generated files provide the client and server class templates
required to implement and call the new ActionsService, which consolidates
state and execution management for actions (replacing previous StateService
and QueueService patterns). Keeping the generated stubs in tree enables
service integration and local development until the service implementations
are provided.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* Fix Docker build for CGO-dependent sqlite3 package

The build was failing because `go-sqlite3` requires CGO, but the
Dockerfile used cross-compilation (`--platform=${BUILDPLATFORM}`) which
disables CGO. Additionally, the .dockerignore negation pattern for
`gen/go` was unreliable when the parent `gen/` directory was excluded.

- Remove cross-compilation, enable CGO_ENABLED=1 for native build
- Copy only gen/go instead of full gen directory
- Replace .dockerignore negation with explicit subdirectory exclusions

* [V2] Fix trace issue (#7178)

* fix(runs): persist model CreatedAt in CreateAction for correct trace ordering

Trace actions set CreatedAt to the span's start_time so that parents
(which start before children but are recorded later) sort earlier in
ListActions ORDER BY created_at ASC. The INSERT was omitting created_at,
causing the DB to use CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (insert time) and reversing the
parent/child order — leading to "parent node not found" errors in
WatchActions when a child action was processed before its parent.

Non-trace actions leave CreatedAt as the zero value and fall back to
time.Now(), preserving existing behaviour.

* [V2] Expand contextutils with org, service_name, cluster_id keys and logKeys (#7229)

* [V2] Expand contextutils with org, service_name, cluster_id keys and logKeys

The shared interceptor chain in Union Cloud sets context values using v1
contextutils.Key types, but v2 services (actions, leaseworker, leasor,
events-proxy, executorv2) use the v2 logger which reads v2 contextutils.Key.
Both are `type Key string` but are different Go types, so context.Value()
lookups fail silently and all context-propagated log fields are missing from
v2 service logs.

Add OrganizationKey, ServiceNameKey, and ClusterNameKey constants to v2
contextutils, and expand logKeys with ProjectKey, DomainKey, and the three
new keys so that GetLogFields() includes them in structured log output.

This is one half of the fix — the other half is a context bridge interceptor
in the cloud repo that copies v1 values onto v2 keys at request time.

* fix(flytek8s): surface init-container waiting failures in DemystifyPending (#7244)

Port of unionai/flyte#956 to v2. Fixes indefinite task hang when an init
container is stuck (e.g. ImagePullBackOff on a missing init image,
InvalidImageName, CreateContainerConfigError).

demystifyPendingHelper now inspects InitContainerStatuses before
ContainerStatuses, so the real init-container failure surfaces with the
correct reason and per-reason grace-period handling. Previously, the main
container's downstream Waiting{PodInitializing} masked the init-container
failure; only the coarse PodPendingTimeout would eventually rescue the task.

The waiting-reason switch is extracted into classifyWaitingContainer
(byte-equivalent logic move, preserving v2's existing classification for
CreateContainerError / CreateContainerConfigError past grace).

refactor(gpufault): the fault relevance window lives with the contract

Whether a fault was firing close enough to a failure to explain it is part of what
a GPU fault means, not a detail of how the executor reads events. Keeping it in
the executor meant the next consumer had to copy it, and one already has: the
leaseworker in unionai/cloud carries its own transcription of the same interval
arithmetic and the same two durations, which is two places to get the aggregated
event case wrong.

RelevantToFailure and the two durations it reads move into gpufault, which is
already the one definition of the fault contract. It takes plain times rather than
the executor's cached event type, so the package stays free of executor imports
and any consumer with a first-recorded and a last-observed time can ask the
question. The semantics are unchanged: a fault is active from when it was first
recorded until it was last seen, either time standing in for the other when one is
missing, and it explains a failure when that stretch overlaps the window before
the failure and the small slack after it.

The executor keeps its tests. They go through classifyGpuFailure rather than
calling the check directly, so they still earn their place: they are what catches
the executor handing the two times over in the wrong order, which the new
unit tests in gpufault cannot see.

fix: rename the template's task container to what the operator expects

Follow-up on the entrypoint fix, addressing three things about the first
version.

Rename the container. The operator's mutating webhook patches the
container it finds by name -- spark-kubernetes-driver, or
executor/spark-kubernetes-executor -- and leaves the pod alone when none
matches (findContainer in internal/webhook/sparkpod_defaulter.go). Under
the task's own container name every volume, mount and env the operator
manages is dropped. The plugin already assumed the driver name elsewhere:
its log links and DemystifyFailedOrPendingPod both look for
defaultDriverPrimaryContainerName in the pod, which nothing produced.

Scope the rewrite to Flyte's own pod spec. A custom driver/executor pod
spec is written against what the operator generates, so it already
carries these names and never the task entrypoint. It stays verbatim,
now structurally rather than by the name lookup happening to miss.

Tie the names to the operator's constants instead of a literal, so the
rename, the log links and the webhook cannot drift apart.

feat(executor): classify GPU faults recorded on a CRD task's child pods

Classification so far covered tasks whose tracked resource is the Pod itself. A
RayJob, PyTorchJob, MPIJob or TFJob records the Xid on a worker pod while the
executor tracks the CRD, so the fault the node saw never reached the failure the
user read, and a GPU that fell off the bus during distributed training still
looked like the workload's own crash.

Nothing new has to be watched to fix that. The event informer is not scoped to
the tracked resource, so a worker pod's events are already cached, and the Pod
informer is already running and already selects on the managed label that every
plugin merges into the pod templates it builds. What was missing was a way to
name the pods: an operator's child pod names carry a random suffix, so the
executor cannot derive the keys the events are cached under.

ChildPodDiscovery is the optional interface that closes that, in the shape
PluginAbortOverride already established. A plugin returns the label selector that
picks out this attempt's pods; the manager lists them from the resource's own
namespace out of the cache it already holds, and reads each one's faults. Because
the pods arrive as objects, their UIDs are known, so the identity check that
already guarded the Pod path applies unchanged and never has to fall back to
matching on a name.

AttemptPodSelector builds the half of that selector which holds whichever
operator created the pod. The run, action and attempt labels move to flytek8s
next to the managed label, for the reason that one already lives there: the
plugins that build pod templates have to keep them intact. It refuses to build a
selector when any of them is missing, since run and action are dropped when
sanitization empties them and selecting on what is left would reach another
action's pods. PreservedPodLabels exposes the same key set for plugins to
re-apply after any labels a user supplied, so that the two halves cannot disagree
about which labels have to survive.

Which pods are consulted is narrower than everything the selector matches. A
worker that finished its work cannot be why the job failed, so a succeeded pod
contributes nothing even if it logged a fault mid-run; crediting that to a
launcher's user-code failure would turn a user error into a hardware one and stop
charging the retry. A pod still running is kept, because a worker wedged on a GPU
that fell off the bus is exactly the case this path exists for.

Relevance is anchored per pod on that pod's own container termination, because
every CRD plugin stamps the failure with the time of the reconcile that noticed
it rather than with anything the kubelet recorded, and anchoring on the reconcile
would age out a fault that killed a worker minutes earlier. Init containers are
not eligible anchors: they finish before the workload starts, and a native
sidecar declared among them is reaped after everything else. The anchor is never
later than the attempt's own failure, so a pod torn down long afterwards cannot
let faults recorded in the meantime explain it.

Which fault wins needs no new rule: ClassifyFailure already takes the worst
severity and the earliest within it, so the faults gathered across pods are only
sorted back into order before being handed over. That order is on when each fault
was first recorded rather than when it was last seen, because a fault that is
still repeating has a later last observation than a one-shot fault that followed
it, and ordering on that would let a downstream symptom outrank the root cause.
The last observation still decides relevance, which is all it was ever for.

The one pod whose fault settled the verdict is named as an additional reason,
because the fault sentence carries the Xid, the GPU and the node but not the pod,
which on a job with sixty-four workers is not enough to act on. Only that pod is
named: pointing at every pod that saw any fault would put a misleading reason on
a failure the faults did not explain, and would emit one cluster event per pod
when a whole node's worth of GPUs faults at once. The single pod path names
nothing, since the failure is already reported against that pod.

A gang-scheduled restart creates fresh pods under the same attempt and its faults
count, while an earlier Flyte attempt's pods are excluded by the attempt label. A
plugin that does not implement the interface contributes no pods and so no
faults, which is exactly what it did before.

A pod already torn down with its job is not recovered. The events are cached
under a name nothing can reconstruct, so discovery logs at debug and classifies
nothing rather than guessing.

refactor(executor): count active TaskActions from cache indexer (no deep-copy)

The taskaction.active gauge listed CRDs via client.List on every metrics
collection, which deep-copies every TaskAction out of the informer cache.
At high CRD counts that is O(N) full-object copies plus GC churn each cycle.

Read straight from the SharedIndexInformer's indexer instead: indexer.List()
returns the cached object pointers without copying. Extract a pure countByPhase
tally and inject it via cachedPhaseCounter(mgr.GetCache()), which also decouples
registerTaskActionMetrics from the client and simplifies its test.

feat(chart): add headless webhook service for cache invalidation fanout

A ClusterIP Service load-balances to exactly one pod, so invalidating through
it would leave every other replica serving stale secrets until TTL. The
headless Service resolves to all pod IPs, which is what a fan-out caller
needs.

Added alongside the existing webhook Service rather than converting it: that
one is what the MutatingWebhookConfiguration points the API server at for
admission and has to keep its ClusterIP. Cloud does the same — a separate
flyte-pod-webhook-headless next to flyte-pod-webhook.

Inert until the webhook runs with more than one replica; the client still
targets the single configured URL. Noted at the call site, including why
repointing the URL at the headless name without fan-out code is worse than
leaving it alone.

feat(copilot): preserve nested subdirectories in multipart blob uploads

Uploader.handleBlobType built each file's storage key from info.Name()
(basename only) and skipped directories with a warning. Files written into
subdirectories of a Dir/MULTIPART output were therefore flattened to their
basename on upload — and because uploads run as concurrent futures, two files
sharing a basename across different subdirs (e.g. a/dup.txt and b/dup.txt)
would nondeterministically overwrite each other, silently losing data.

Walk into directories and key each file by its relative path from the blob
root (filepath.Rel + ConstructReference with the path segments), mirroring the
download side, which already reconstructs nested keys. Top-level files are
unaffected — their relative path is just the basename, so keys are unchanged.

Add an upload-multipart-nested test covering a root file, nested files, and a
cross-subdir basename collision.

Datacatalog cache

Add DedupingBucketRateLimiter

Our use of a `BucketRateLimiter` with `DelayingQueue` is problematic when repeatedly inserting the same items. The former continually moves out the rate limit token time with each new item (no deduping), while the latter dedupes insertions. The net effect is that under load newly inserted items end up with a token time way in the future while the queue happily drains to empty with items processed at a much lower than expected rate.

This PR adds a new `DedupingBucketRateLimiter` that maintains historic reservations per item and skips taking out a new reservation when a duplicate item is found with an outstanding reservation. Reservations are dropped from the map when `Forget` is called, which happens after the item is fully processed. This is similar to how the exponential backoff rate limiter works. See [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/client-go/blob/master/util/workqueue/default_rate_limiters.go#L82-L149).

- [x] Run new rate limiter under high execution load and verify that queue is kept full but not overflown.

feat(flyte-binary): add optional JWT and auth-discovery ingresses

On ingress controllers like AWS ALB, a single ingress can't combine cookie-OIDC
(browser) and JWT (token) auth, nor expose unauthenticated auth-discovery paths
alongside auth-gated ones. Previously these were hand-rolled as out-of-band
kubectl ingresses. This makes them first-class, opt-in chart resources so the
whole dual-auth topology is reproducible from the chart.

- templates/ingress/api-jwt.yaml: optional ingress (ingress.apiJwtIngress.enabled)
  that serves the shared apiPaths backed by the http service. Intended for a
  higher controller precedence + a "Authorization: Bearer*" match condition +
  JWT validation, supplied via annotations. Reuses ingress.apiPaths, so all API
  services (including RunLogsService) are JWT-validated for Bearer clients.
- templates/ingress/wellknown.yaml: optional ingress
  (ingress.wellknownIngress.enabled) for the unauthenticated auth-discovery paths
  (/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, AuthMetadataService, IdentityService,
  SettingsService) via the new ingress.wellknownPaths helper.
- values.yaml: ingress.apiJwtIngress.* and ingress.wellknownIngress.* — both
  disabled by default; annotations/ingressClassName are pass-through.
- README.md: regenerate the new parameter rows.

Both render only when ingress.create is also true.

feat(actions): report where a running action can be reached (ActionAddress)

Some actions serve traffic while they run, such as an interactive sandbox
session: the code that started it needs to reach it as soon as it is ready,
not when it finishes.

IDL:
- flyteidl2.common.ActionAddress { pod { namespace, name, ip, port }, path,
  url, cluster }: a pod serving the action plus the path that reaches it;
  url only for an endpoint not derivable from the pod (gateway, tunnel).
- actions.UpdateRequest.address (write side) and a new
  workflow.ActionUpdate.address (read side, on WatchForUpdates).
- core.WorkerKind.WORKER_KIND_MICROVM for tasks that each run in their own
  microVM (interactive sessions), distinct from WORKER_KIND_SANDBOX.

OSS actions service (Kubernetes-backed): TaskAction.status.address in the
CRD; PutStatus stores it (kept by updates without one, replaced by a new
one, cleared by a new attempt or a terminal phase), separate from the
signal value; watchers get it live and in the initial snapshot while the
action is not terminal.

fix(flyteplugins): report a pod the cluster disrupted as a system failure

A pod preempted by a scheduler, drained or removed by the taint manager
or pod GC carries the DisruptionTarget condition. Plain pod tasks
ignored it: a preempted pod exits 143 after SIGTERM and was classified
as a user failure, and one caught while terminating only read as
UnexpectedObjectDeletion.

Match DisruptionTarget in GetTerminationTarget next to Kueue's
TerminationTarget, so both DemystifyFailure and
classifyExternalTermination report the reason and treat it as a system
failure. TerminationByKubelet is left out, since it also marks
node-pressure evictions the task can cause itself.

Fixes #8067

fix(clustered): scope JobSet log context pod list to own namespace and jobset-name label

getLogContext listed pods through the executor's cluster-wide K8sReader without a namespace or label filter, assuming K8sReader was already scoped to the node execution. While a JobSet's rank-0 pod was Pending, the action's log context fell back to the first non-Pending pod in the cluster-wide cache — often another run's pod — causing flyte get logs and the console log panel to stream another run's logs.

Scope the K8sReader.List call in getLogContext by namespace and the jobset.sigs.k8s.io/jobset-name label stamped by the JobSet controller, so a JobSet whose pods are all Pending returns no log context until one of its own pods starts.

Add Secret.env_var support into union secrets (#632)

## Overview
Adds the `Secrets.env_var` to union secrets.

## Test Plan
I updated this PR with unit tests to cover the changes.

I deployed to serverless-staging and ran the following to check that the env var points to the value and the file.

```
from flytekit import task, Secret, ImageSpec
from typing import Optional
import os

image = ImageSpec(
    apt_packages=["git"],
    packages=[
        "union",
    ],
    builder="default",
    registry="ghcr.io/thomasjpfan",
    commands=[
        "uv pip install git+https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte.git@ab463c3c8297b525bb73e7735f6bac1cf884092b#subdirectory=flyteidl",
        "uv pip install git+https://github.com/thomasjpfan/flytekit.git@8814da92a8578dbad07550486a5aaced5785d7a5",
    ],
)


@task(
    container_image=image,
    secret_requests=[
        Secret(
            key="thomasjpfan-secret",
            mount_requirement=Secret.MountType.ENV_VAR,
            env_var="HELLO_WORLD",
        )
    ],
)
def get_secret_env_var() -> Optional[str]:
    return os.getenv("HELLO_WORLD")


@task(
    container_image=image,
    secret_requests=[
        Secret(
            key="thomasjpfan-secret",
            mount_requirement=Secret.MountType.FILE,
            env_var="HELLO_WORLD",
        )
    ],
)
def get_secret_file() -> str:
    with open(os.getenv("HELLO_WORLD"), "r") as f:
        return f.read()
```

perf(runs): don't block action writes on the NOTIFY pump

notifyActionUpdate and notifyRunUpdate did a blocking send on a 256-slot
channel from inside write RPCs, right after the row was already committed.
Once the pump fell behind, a best-effort wakeup turned into user-visible
write latency, and a cancelled request context discarded the notification
outright, leaving other watchers on a stale phase.

Replace the FIFO channels with a mutex-guarded pending set per notification
kind plus a capacity-1 signal channel. The writer inserts a key and nudges
the pump without ever blocking; the pump swaps the sets out and emits them.
Because a payload is an identity and every listener re-reads state from the
database when woken, repeated updates for one action collapse into a single
delivery, and memory is bounded by distinct pending actions rather than by
update volume.

A failed pg_notify merges its keys back into the pending set and retries with
backoff instead of dropping them, so a transient database problem costs a
delay rather than a lost wakeup. Two limits keep that retry from becoming a
new failure mode. A payload only spends its retry budget when the connection
was healthy and it failed anyway, which is what happens to a payload Postgres
will never accept, such as one of 8000 bytes or more; after enough of those
attempts it is dropped with an error. And a drain that delivered anything
resets the backoff, so one bad payload cannot slow every other watcher down.

A lost connection aborts the current drain so the remaining payloads do not
each trigger their own reconnect attempt.

Stop treating a gracefully-deleting pod as an unexpected failure (#8112)

fix(executor): don't fail a gracefully-deleting pod as unexpected

checkResourcePhase reported any non-terminal object with a
DeletionTimestamp as UnexpectedObjectDeletion, a SYSTEM-retryable
failure. A pod under a graceful delete carries that timestamp and
stays non-terminal for its whole grace period, so the branch fired
continuously, not once.

That drove the controller to reset plugin state and recreate a pod
under the same name on every reconcile, colliding with the
still-terminating original (Create returning AlreadyExists) and
livelocking at API speed. MaxSystemFailures never bounded it because
the counter reset on the AlreadyExists-driven Queued transition every
lap.

Drop the branch and let the object be observed until it is actually
gone, at which point the existing NotFound handling above already
produces ResourceDeletedExternally.

The branch came from v1 propeller, where it caught pods that would
never finish deleting: a vanished kubelet leaves them Running with a
DeletionTimestamp, held by the flyte finalizer. v1 recovered by
starting a new attempt under a new pod name and clearing the old
pod's finalizer. v2 does neither, so the branch never recovered
anything here: if the object still exists, the same-name relaunch
livelocks (a stuck pod livelocks forever); if it is already gone,
the NotFound path reaches the same system retry one reconcile later.
Gating the branch on the deletion deadline would only postpone the
livelock to the stuck case. A pod stuck in deletion now waits for the
task timeout instead of looping.

Fixes #8066 (fix 1 of the proposed fixes; fixes 2-4 are hardening for
the quota/backoff and AlreadyExists/counter-reset symptoms and are not
included here).

fix(webhook): replace invalid namespaced owner reference with labels

MutatingWebhookConfiguration is a cluster-scoped resource. Setting
OwnerReferences from a namespaced Pod violates Kubernetes rules: in
v1.20+ the reference is silently ignored, leaving the webhook config
orphaned on uninstall.

Replace the OwnerReferences copy with labels that track the managing
pod's name and namespace for identification without violating the
cluster-scoped/namespaced boundary.

Closes #6692

Ensure that k8s plugins (dask, kfoperator) have resource requests and limits set (#664)

## Overview
Perennial recently ran into an issue where they specified dask scheduler and worker resource requests but not limits.

It turns out in the container task (and k8s pod task) we automatically adjust resource requests and limits such that if one is unset, then we substitute a value from the other, or the overall platform values set in the task execution metadata.

This isn't the case for other k8s operators. This change updates this.

## Test Plan
Using this workflow
```
@task(
    task_config=Dask(
        workers=WorkerGroup(
            number_of_workers=10,
            requests=Resources(cpu="4", mem="10Gi"),
        ),
    ),
    requests=Resources(cpu="1", mem="2Gi"),
    container_image=custom_image,
)
def hello_dask(size: int) -> float:
    array = da.random.random(size)
    return float(array.mean().compute())
```

fix: close HTTP response bodies and file handles to prevent resource leaks

Several resource leaks found across the codebase:

1. flyteadmin/auth/authzserver/metadata_provider.go:
   - HTTP response body from OAuth2 metadata fetch was never closed
   - On retry with 4xx/5xx status, previous response body was leaked

2. flytectl/cmd/register/register_util.go:
   - HTTP response body from DirectUpload was never closed

3. flytectl/pkg/filesystemutils/file_system_utils.go:
   - File handle leaked on non-EOF io.CopyN error during tar extraction

4. flytestdlib/config/viper/collection.go:
   - Config file reader was never closed after MergeConfig

Fix array node eventing (#807)

Previously, when flyteworkflow CR updates failed causing for taskPhaseVersion to fall out of date, array node subnode events would be dropped as admin and a propeller side filter prevent duplicate events from being sent. To fix this, we [added retries and increment task phase version](https://github.com/unionai/flyte/pull/421/files#diff-67941e1320bd66fda570ebcf1f1c5c5221d608b136d662705e168a07a5d166ef). However, this presents issues when many updates fail in a row causes the taskPhaseVersion falls behind the number of retries + increments guaranteeing failure (as we see many times w/ Woven).

Instead, we opt for eventual subnode phase consistency when ArrayNode reaches a terminal state. When an array node reaches terminal state, we send an event that includes external resources that have all the subnode phases. Admin will merge the updated phase into a matching existing index or create a new one.

Note there is an additional tradeoff to the arraynode subnode state being potentially incorrect while the parent array node is running:
- if all the events that included updates for a particular subnode failed, we would lose logs and metadata for that given subnode but still have subnode phase correct

Fail the install when copilotStorageSecretRef cannot take effect

The value asks the chart to point co-pilot at an existing Secret, but the key
it feeds (plugins.k8s.co-pilot.storage-config-secret-name) is emitted by the
chart-rendered ConfigMap, and externalConfigMap/externalSecretRef replace that
ConfigMap wholesale. Setting both left co-pilot on the command-line fallback
while the operator had every reason to believe the credentials were now in a
Secret, which is the wrong way round for a security setting to fail.

The chart cannot paper over it: in external mode the operator owns the storage
configuration, so the chart has no way to build the Secret or set the key for
them. Reject the combination instead, and say which key to set by hand.

Validation lives in a helper called from deployment.yaml, which renders even
when the ConfigMap and Secret templates are switched off. Renders are
byte-identical for every valid combination.

fix(runs): chunk multi-row InsertEvents under Postgres bind-parameter cap

InsertEvents is not only fed by the executor's batcher (<=400 events/flush):
RecordActionEvents accepts arbitrary event counts, and a single multi-row
INSERT tops out at Postgres' 65,535 bind parameters (9 per row -> 7,281 rows),
failing the whole request beyond that. Insert in 5,000-row chunks — same
non-transactional semantics as the previous per-row loop, ON CONFLICT DO
NOTHING keeps retries idempotent. Adds TestInsertEvents_ChunksOversizedBatch
(8,000 events, forcing multiple chunks).

wip

Render the co-pilot Secret only when there is a credential to protect

The gate asked whether the chart could render a complete storage config, not
whether that config held anything secret. So S3 with authType=iam, GCS (whose
json key the chart hardcodes empty), and Azure without a key all got a Secret
and a projected volume on every task pod to protect a region and an endpoint.

Gate on the credential instead: S3 accesskey with a literal secretKey, Azure
with a key, or an operator-supplied Secret. Ambient auth stays on the command
line, where nothing sensitive travels.

configuration.inline.storage also qualifies, whatever it holds. The chart
cannot see whether an operator put a session token or a service-account key in
there, and config-secret.yaml merges it into the Secret, so the safe default is
the Secret. secretKeyPath is unchanged: it is credential-bearing but unreadable
at template time, so it stays on the command line.

Verified the Secret and the plugin key appear or vanish together for every
combination, since a mismatch strands task pods in ContainerCreating.

docs: Add clarification on required Kafka version field in cloud_events configuration for FlyteAdmin (#6502)

The current documentation for the FlyteAdmin cloudEvents Kafka configuration does not mention that the `version` field under the `kafka` block is required. 

If this field is omitted, attempting to start FlyteAdmin with Kafka cloud events enabled leads to a panic error with the message "caught panic: invalid version".

An example of a minimal valid configuration is as follows:
```
cloudEvents:
  enable: true
  kafka:
    brokers: 127.0.0.1:9092
    version: my-kafka-version
  eventsPublisher:
    eventTypes:
      - all
    topicName: myTopic
  type: kafka
```
This change aims to help users avoid runtime errors and improve the ease of adoption for this feature.

fix(flyte-binary): default task-pod control-plane callback env vars

Task pods call back to the control plane to enqueue child actions and
watch state. With no config the SDK falls back to the devbox default
host.docker.internal:8090, which doesn't resolve in a real cluster, so
every action fails its retries and the controller recreates the pod in a
loop — runs never complete.

Inject the three env vars the devbox already uses into every task pod by
default, with the endpoint computed from this release's in-cluster HTTP
service (so it's correct for any fullnameOverride/namespace):
  _U_EP_OVERRIDE=<release>-http.<ns>:8090
  _U_INSECURE=true        # in-cluster service is plain HTTP
  _U_USE_ACTIONS=1        # actions/queue path

Overridable via configuration.inline.plugins.k8s.default-env-vars.

Fix project status change on update for archived projects (#438)

Before, updating some field (i.e. `Description`) of an `Archived` project causes the project state to
change to `Active`. This is caused by a bug in the `updateProjectsFunc` function used for the `update` command.

During project updates, `edited`, a default project created based on the given configs/flags,
comes with `admin.Project_ACTIVE` state by default if both `activate` and `archive` flags 
have not been set. 

Then a `copy` of the target project will be updated based on `edited` and then used for showing
the diff. In the current implementation, the state of the `copy` is set to be the same as `edited` 
projects state, which is `Project_ACTIVE` if no flags are set.

Also, after showing the diff, the `edited` is used for updating the project. Since it comes
with `Project_ACTIVE` state by default, the target project will be updated to have `Project_ACTIVE`
if both `activate` and `archive` flags are unset, regardless of the projects previous state.

On this PR, we make sure we set the correct state to both `copy` and `edited` by checking 
if  both `activate` and `archive` flags are set/unset. If one of the flags are set, we update target
project state (`copy`) based on the `edited` state since it will have the desired state. If both
flags are unset, we set the `edited` state to be the same as target (`copy`) state. This way, updating
`archived` projects will not change their state.

fix(executor): run an initial TaskAction GC sweep on startup

GarbageCollector.Start used time.NewTicker, whose first tick fires only after a
full interval (default 30m). So the first collection was always deferred by the
whole interval, and any restart that arrived sooner than the interval reset the
ticker before it ever fired -- terminal TaskActions then accumulated without
bound (observed ~19k Completed CRDs on a frequently-redeployed dev cluster, none
collected).

Run gc.collect once immediately before entering the ticker loop so a fresh start
sweeps right away. Regression test: with a long interval (ticker won't fire),
Start must still delete an expired TaskAction via the initial sweep.

fix(dataproxy): return scheme-qualified ClusterEndpoint from SelectCluster

SelectCluster returned the bare Host header (e.g. development.uniondemo.run).
The console uses ClusterEndpoint directly as a Connect transport base URL, and a
scheme-less value is treated by the browser as a relative path — resolved against
the current page — so GetActionData 404'd at
/v2/.../runs/development.uniondemo.run/flyteidl2.dataproxy.DataProxyService/GetActionData.

Qualify the host with a scheme: prefer X-Forwarded-Proto (set by any TLS-terminating
proxy/LB — the dev cluster ALB sets https), and default to http when absent so a
direct local devbox (no proxy, http) still works.

fix(secret): accept a scheme-less webhookURL

url.Parse reads "webhook-headless.flyte.svc:9444" as scheme
"webhook-headless.flyte.svc" with opaque "9444" and an empty Host, so the
no-host guard rejected every scheme-less form -- "localhost", "localhost:9444",
and the service-name form someone would most plausibly hand-write.

The failure was quiet: invalidation is best-effort, so a rejected URL only
logged a warning and left secrets stale until the 24h TTL while writes kept
succeeding.

Default the scheme to http when the value has none.

Give the system retry event a version the store can keep

Two defects the devbox found that the unit tests could not. Action events are
stored under (action, attempt, phase, version) and a duplicate key is dropped
on insert, so the retry event, which keeps its attempt and reports the Queued
phase the launch events already used, was discarded and the preemption stayed
invisible. It now takes its version from a range plugins never reach, under
the signed 32-bit ceiling the column imposes.

A failure to publish it no longer holds the attempt back either: the event
only explains the retry, and returning early on it left the action reconciling
the same dead pod forever.

Change Flyte CR naming scheme to better support namespace_mapping

 - Typically Flyte is configured so that each project / domain has its
   own Kubernetes namespace.

   Certain environments may change this behavior by using the Flyteadmin
   namespace_mapping setting to put all executions in fewer (or a singular)
   Kubernetes namespace. This is problematic because it can lead to
   collisions in the naming of the CR that flyteadmin generates.

 - This patch fixes 2 important things to make this work properly inside
   of Flyte:

   * it adds a random element to the CR name in Flyte so that the CR is
     named by the execution + some unique value when created by
     flyteadmin

     Without this change, an execution Foo in project A will prevent an
     execution Foo in project B from launching, because the name of the
     CR thats generated in Kubernetes *assumes* that the namespace the
     CRs are put into is different for project A and project B

     When namespace_mapping is set to a singular value, that assumption
     is wrong

   * it makes sure that when flytepropeller cleans up the CR resource
     that it uses Kubernetes labels to find the correct CR -- so instead
     of assuming that it can use the execution name, it instead uses the
     project, domain and execution labels

 - Adds use-workflow-cr-name-suffix setting as a true / false value to
   determine whether to append a deterministic hash of execution id, name,
   project, as the FlyteWorkflow CR name. This uses a fixed length of 10
   which introduces enough entropy to prevent collisions in practical
   terms
