Merge pull request #37 from lyft/backoff

# Namespaced Resource-based Exponential Backoff Handler

Supporting per-namespace resource-aware backoff mechanism to guard pod creation.
Instead of having a separate back off on each execution or having one back off for the entire queue, this PR aims to supports per-namespace backoff which strikes a good balance on the granularity given the resource quota is set per namespace.

This backoff mechanism also is resource-aware. Even if a creation request is blocked and the blocking is still active, the next creation request coming in can be allowed to try if the resource requirement of this creation request is strictly smaller all the previous trials during the same backoff period. This prevents one single big creation request unnecessarily blocking everything else coming from the same namespace.

perf(runs): bump WatchActions snapshot pageSize 100->1000

listAndSendAllActions pages the initial snapshot by OFFSET, which re-scans ~offset
rows per page (cost ~O(n^2/pageSize)). At pageSize=100 an 8,000-action run took ~5s
to stream the full snapshot and raced the console's ~5.5s stream timeout, so large
runs were truncated (showed ~4.6K of 8K after refresh). Raising the page size ~10x
cuts scanned rows and round trips, bringing the snapshot well under a second.

A keyset (cursor) pagination follow-up will make this O(n) for arbitrarily large runs.

Add ArtifactService.ListArtifactNames

Lists distinct artifact names within a project — one ArtifactGroup per name
carrying the latest version's full record plus the total version count,
ordered by the latest version's creation time (newest first). Token
pagination and the name CONTAINS filter ride the common.ListRequest.

ListArtifacts pages over individual versions, so building a grouped
per-name view client-side is O(total versions) and cannot produce correct
version counts; this pushes the grouping to the service where it is one
indexed query.

## Overview
For managed+ customers to seamlessly migrate to using new secrets, we need to allow new secrets to be used side by side with old secret managers.

- adds a new configuration `secretManagerTypes`, which allows specifying multiple secret managers that would be executed in the order specified
- adds logic to loop through all specified secret managers.

Deployed to dogfood and tested with both single and multiple secret managers side by side.

Making ArrayNode taskPhaseVersion increment retries configurable (#698) (#6374)

This PR makes the ArrayNode `taskPhaseVersion` increment retries configurable. This value is used to resend `TaskExecutionEvents` in the case of ArrayNode eventing failures. It is necessary because ArrayNode uses the `ExternalResourceInfo` fields to populate subNode execution metadata, all of these are included in a singular event. So the `TaskPhaseVersion` is not necessarily correlated to a single phase (as subNode phases can change). To ensure these are populated we need to increment.

The default value is the current value (ie. 3) so there should be no concerns about merging.

This will be rolled out immediately using the `managed-cluster-*` pipelines.

feat(copilot): add NAMED_DIR file input layout to preserve filenames (#7534)

* feat(copilot): add NAMED_DIR file input layout to preserve filenames

CoPilot stages File and list[File] inputs at extensionless paths
(/var/inputs/<var> for a single File, /var/inputs/<var>/<index> for
list elements), which breaks tools that sniff format by extension —
e.g. salmon rejects a gzipped FASTQ staged as "0" ("has extension ,
neither a fasta nor a fastq").

Add an opt-in DataLoadingConfig.file_input_layout enum
{DIRECT=0 (default) | NAMED_DIR=1}. DIRECT is the existing behavior,
so raw ContainerTasks are unaffected. Under NAMED_DIR the downloader
stages each File input into a per-input directory under its ORIGINAL
basename (recovered from the blob URI, which the SDK preserves on
upload), so names and extensions round-trip end-to-end:

  fasta : File        -> /var/inputs/fasta/genome.fasta
  reads : list[File]  -> /var/inputs/reads/sample_R1.fastq.gz
                         /var/inputs/reads/sample_R2.fastq.gz

list[File] elements that share a basename are de-duplicated with an
index prefix (1_reads.fastq.gz) so colliding names never clobber.
Dir inputs are multipart blobs and are untouched by the flag.

Consumers glob /var/inputs/<var>/* to read File/list[File] inputs.

- flyteidl2/core/tasks.proto: add FileInputLayout enum +
  DataLoadingConfig.file_input_layout field; regenerate Go bindings
- flytecopilot/data/download.go: per-input-dir staging under NAMED_DIR
  for single File and list[File], with basename collision dedup
- flytecopilot/cmd/download.go: --file-input-layout flag (empty=DIRECT)
- flyteplugins/.../flytek8s/copilot.go: thread pilot.GetFileInputLayout()
  into the downloader's --file-input-layout arg
- tests updated across data/, cmd/, and flytek8s/ for the new behavior

fix(flytek8s): classify ImagePullBackOff caused by registry 429 as system error

Container runtimes surface registry rate limiting (HTTP 429 Too Many
Requests) through the ImagePullBackOff waiting reason. Today, once the
ImagePullBackoffGracePeriod elapses, DemystifyPending returns
PhaseInfoRetryableFailureWithCleanup, which is classified as a USER
error and consumes the user's retry budget.

429s from the registry are an infrastructure problem outside the user's
control — typically a transient throttling event on the registry side.
Detect the "429 Too Many Requests" substring in the waiting message and
route those cases to PhaseInfoSystemRetryableFailureWithCleanup so they
do not exhaust the user's retries.

All other ImagePullBackOff messages keep their existing user-error
classification.

refactor(flytek8s): export the failure anchor a fault is judged against

Working out when a pod's trouble actually happened is the other half of deciding
whether a GPU fault explains a failure, and it was still private to the executor.
The leaseworker in unionai/cloud is now adopting the relevance check, so without
this it would carry a second copy that has to move in lockstep with the first.

PodFailureTime moves to flytek8s, which is where pod inspection already lives, and
lands next to GetLastTransitionOccurredAt on purpose: that function is the reason
this one exists. It reports the latest transition across every container including
the init containers, so for a pod that failed while its containers were still
running it hands back the time the container started. Anchoring a six-hour task on
its own start puts every real fault outside the window. PodFailureTime takes the
latest terminated main container instead, then the deletion timestamp an eviction
leaves behind, and only then whatever time the caller already had.

It stays out of gpufault, which has no Kubernetes imports and should keep none.
phaseInfoOccurredAt stays in the executor: it reads a PhaseInfo, not a pod, and
nothing outside the plugin machinery has one.

The table tests move with the function and gained the cases that were awkward to
reach through the executor, including one asserting the divergence from
GetLastTransitionOccurredAt that motivates the whole helper. The executor keeps
its end-to-end test for the evicted pod, which is what catches the anchor being
wired up wrong rather than computed wrong.

Return non-0 exit code from copilot upload failure

 - The current copilot behavior is to:

   * try to upload the specified file
   * if an error occurs, try to write an error file instead
     * if the error file write succeeds, return success -- otherwise error

   This behavior is not ideal, because it suppresses real issues like
   the inability to find the expected output file. While a case can be
   made that the sidecar succeeded in handling its responsibility,
   important information is lost in the process that is useful to other
   containers in the job.

   Generallyk, it's better to consider the inability to
   find the original file a failure of the job to produce the expected
   file in the expected location (useful especially for container tasks).
   That means that a failure to upload the file should also return a
   non-0 exit code.

 - The new behavior is therefore:

   * try to upload the specified file
   * if an error occurs, try to write an error file instead
     * if the error file write succeeds, return the original error
     * if the error file write fails, return a joined version of the
       errors

Add Kubernetes event metadata to ClusterEvent and ReasonInfo

ClusterEvent gains type (Normal/Warning), reason (e.g. FailedMount, BackOff),
source_component (e.g. kubelet), and observed occurrence count, instead of
carrying only a free-text message. This lets consoles distinguish warnings
from routine events, show the machine-readable reason, and collapse repeats.

ReasonInfo in the plugin machinery gains an optional KubernetesEvent
(K8sEventMetadata) so executors that attach k8s object events to task phase
info can forward the structured metadata alongside the message.

Additive and backward compatible; generated code refreshed via make gen.

Add list Datasets endpoint (#25)

* Add list Datasets endpoint

perf(runs): keyset-paginate the WatchActions snapshot (O(n))

OFFSET paging (even at pageSize 1000) is O(n^2/pageSize): each page re-scans ~offset
rows, so a 32k-action run's snapshot took longer than the console's stream timeout and
was truncated (showed ~11k of 32k). Replace it with keyset (cursor) pagination on
(created_at, name) ascending: each page continues strictly after the previous page's
last (created_at, name), so the full snapshot is O(n).

- ListResourceInput gains KeysetAfterCreatedAt/KeysetAfterName; ListActions emits the
  Postgres row-value keyset `(created_at, name) > (?, ?)` (mutually exclusive with
  CursorToken/Offset).
- New index idx_actions_run_created_name (project, domain, run_name, created_at, name)
  turns each page into an index range-scan (created plain, not CONCURRENTLY, since
  migrations run in a transaction).
- created_at stays the primary sort so parents insert before children; name is the
  unique per-run tiebreaker giving a total order, so keyset pages never skip/overlap
  even when a map task bulk-creates thousands of children with identical created_at.

Adds TestListActions_KeysetPagination (tied created_at, full coverage + total order).

fix: always call writeOutput on connector SUCCEEDED to support file-based outputs (#7135)

When a connector task succeeds but returns nil outputs (relying on
file-based outputs written to remote storage), writeOutput was skipped
entirely, leaving the BufferedOutputWriter without a reader. This caused
ValidateOutput to fail with "Outputs not generated by task execution".

Always call writeOutput on SUCCEEDED so the RemoteFileOutputReader
fallback is used when outputs are nil, matching v1 behavior.

fix(executor): honor task-level interruptible when the run-level flag is unset (#7885)

The executor read interruptibility only from TaskAction.Spec.Interruptible,
which is populated from the run-level RunSpec. Interruptible set at the
TaskEnvironment, @env.task, or task.override() level serializes into the
embedded TaskTemplate metadata but never reached pod scheduling, so the
plugins.k8s interruptible node affinity and tolerations were not applied.

The task template's metadata now decides interruptibility whenever the
run-level flag is unset; an explicit run-level value still wins.

Add OTLP and sampling to otelutils (#180)

## Overview
This changes adds support for OLTP and sampling to the otelutils tracer provider abstraction.

Adds support for OLTP. This is the recommended replacement for the deprecated jaeger exporter.
> "go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/jaeger" is deprecated: This module is no longer supported. OpenTelemetry dropped support for Jaeger exporter in July 2023. Jaeger officially accepts and recommends using OTLP

OLTP supports grpc and http, which are added as separate exporter types and configs.

Adds initial [sampling](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/go/sampling/) support to the top level open telemetry config. Defaults to parent sampler `always`, but also adds a config for [TraceIdRatioBased](https://pkg.go.dev/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace#TraceIDRatioBased). See [these docs](https://pkg.go.dev/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/trace#ParentBased) for behavior of parent sampler.

## Test Plan
Ran local sandbox with local jaeger all-in-one and verified
- [x] otlpgrpc with parent sampler always 
- [x] otlpgrpc with parent sampler traceid (along with other defaults)
- [x] otlphttp with parent sampler traceid (along with other defaults)

Flyte config
```
❯ docker run --rm -e COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true -p 16686:16686 -p 4317:4317 -p 4318:4318 jaegertracing/all-in-one:1.52
```

Jaeger
```
otel:
  type: otlpgrpc
  sampler:
    parentSampler: traceid
```

## Rollout Plan (if applicable)
This change is a no-op, so limited concerns merging. Next step is to pull into cloud repo, wire up to open telemetry collector, and enable sampling.

Should this change be upstreamed to OSS (flyteorg/flyte)? If so, please check this box for auditing. Note, this is the responsibility of each developer. Add auth enforcement config options (#43)

This is the last bit of auth work on the Admin side of things.  Before this PR, if you present Admin with a bad or expired token, you will get a 401.  However, if you present no token whatsoever, Admin will let the request go through.  This PR begins enforcement.

To help with migration, we are incrementally going to require auth.  We were originally going to use the gRPC endpoint name to decide whether or not to enforce things, but ultimately it made more sense to divide up by protocol - HTTP vs gRPC. Since most programmatic (more problematic) traffic goes through gRPC and only Flyte Console uses HTTP, we can start by just doing HTTP.

In order to do this, the code tags incoming HTTP requests because the token validation code is further downstream.

Also
* Adding the bit of code to look for bearer tokens in http headers as well as cookies to support use-cases where we use the HTTP Admin API.  Note however, that Admin will be deployed with a custom config so that the header you should send is `Flyte-Authorization` not the default `Authorization`, so the complete header would look something like `Flyte-Authorization: Bearer j.w.t`

feat(dataproxy): GetCloudCredentials, short-lived scoped object-store credentials

A signed URL is a capability for ONE object, with the checksum and size the
server chose bound into it. That is the right shape for most uploads and the
wrong one for a client that touches many keys it discovers as it goes: a
mounted Volume reads and writes thousands of chunk keys, and a round trip per
key is not a design. GetCloudCredentials is the other shape -- a capability
over a PREFIX, for a bounded time -- and both now exist so a call site can pick.

The request names a RESOURCE inside a SCOPE, never a path. "Credentials for
s3://bucket/path" is the tempting shape and the wrong one: the server would
have to decide whether this identity may touch that path, which means
inventing a path->resource->authorization mapping and keeping it correct
forever. Keyed by a resource, authorization is the project/domain question the
platform already answers, and the path is an OUTPUT (bucket_uri plus
granted_prefixes). Today's resources are the project's own data area -- the
same place CreateUploadLocation writes -- and a Volume named by its locator.

Three rules hold the security of this together, and all three are enforced in
code rather than documented and hoped for:

1. A resource inside a scope, as above.
2. Every granted prefix must resolve INSIDE that scope. A locator is a path,
   and a path the caller chose is not authorization, so a volume whose data
   lives outside the caller's project/domain is refused rather than vended.
   A locator outside the store's own bucket is refused before the object is
   read at all -- fetching an object because a caller named it is the thing to
   avoid, whatever the object turns out to say.
3. The policy is computed here from the resource. Nothing the client sends can
   widen it: `subpaths` only narrows (and a `..` in one is refused by name),
   and there is no way to pass verbs or a policy.

The mechanism needs NO IAM change in a customer's account. A pod running with
IRSA holds a projected service account token whose role trust already permits
that service account to assume it -- that is what IRSA is -- so exchanging the
same token again with a session Policy asks for nothing new, and a session
policy can only subtract. It is AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity rather than
AssumeRole on purpose: assuming a role from an already-assumed role is role
chaining, which AWS caps at one hour with no way to raise it.

Vending is enabled by what the process IS, not by a flag: NewSTSMinter returns
nil where there is no identity to narrow, and the RPC answers Unimplemented
there instead of pretending. Sessions are cached on (policy, session label) --
together exactly what a credential can do and who it is attributed to -- and
the label lands in RoleSessionName, which is all a CloudTrail reader has to
tell two vended sessions apart, since they all assume the same role.

Measured against real STS and real S3 from a pod with IRSA (the test runs
wherever such an identity exists and skips elsewhere, including CI): a session
scoped to one prefix is refused `ListBucket` on the bucket root with
AccessDenied. That is the assertion no fake can make -- every way of getting a
policy wrong still mints a session and reads its own data perfectly, so a test
that only checks the happy path checks nothing that matters.

Two details that came out of running it rather than reading it:

* The policy deliberately does not grant s3:GetBucketLocation. A session policy
  can only subtract, and a data plane role need not have that verb, so granting
  it would be theatre. The response therefore hands back a region-qualified
  bucket URI, which is what stops a client needing to ask the store where its
  bucket is.
* A Volume's chunks live under its metadata's FORMAT name, not its Volume name:
  a fork copies the format forward while taking a new name, so a fork's chunks
  stay under its ancestor's. A policy built from the name would authenticate
  perfectly and then be denied on the first chunk read. So the client records
  the prefix in the metadata object, and a volume written before that field
  existed is refused with FailedPrecondition rather than scoped wrongly.

OPERATION_GET_CLOUD_CREDENTIALS is added to the cluster SelectCluster
operations so a control plane can route this to the side that owns the store,
exactly as it routes CreateUploadLocation.

Add configuration for launchplan cache resync duration

Currently, the launchplan cache resync duration uses the DownstreamEval duration configuration which is also used for the sync period on the k8s client. This means if we want to configure a more aggressive launchplan cache resync, we would also incur overhead in syncing all k8s resources (ex. Pods from `PodPlugin`). By adding a separate configuration value we can update these independently.

[Flyte 7757] Prevent NOTIFY from blocking action writes (#7965)

* perf(runs): don't block action writes on the NOTIFY pump

notifyActionUpdate and notifyRunUpdate did a blocking send on a 256-slot
channel from inside write RPCs, right after the row was already committed.
Once the pump fell behind, a best-effort wakeup turned into user-visible
write latency, and a cancelled request context discarded the notification
outright, leaving other watchers on a stale phase.

Replace the FIFO channels with a mutex-guarded pending set per notification
kind plus a capacity-1 signal channel. The writer inserts a key and nudges
the pump without ever blocking; the pump swaps the sets out and emits them.
Because a payload is an identity and every listener re-reads state from the
database when woken, repeated updates for one action collapse into a single
delivery, and memory is bounded by distinct pending actions rather than by
update volume.

A failed pg_notify merges its keys back into the pending set and retries with
backoff instead of dropping them, so a transient database problem costs a
delay rather than a lost wakeup. Two limits keep that retry from becoming a
new failure mode. A payload only spends its retry budget when the connection
was healthy and it failed anyway, which is what happens to a payload Postgres
will never accept, such as one of 8000 bytes or more; after enough of those
attempts it is dropped with an error. And a drain that delivered anything
resets the backoff, so one bad payload cannot slow every other watcher down.

A lost connection aborts the current drain so the remaining payloads do not
each trigger their own reconnect attempt.

Fixes #7757

Retry storage operation on all errors

As part of the previous fix, flytecopilot simply initiates a retry (up to 5 max
retries) if a transient error is seen during a flytecopilot raw file upload.
This corresponds to the following list of four specific transient network errors:
 - "http: server closed idle connection"
 - "use of closed network connection"
 - "EOF"
 - "write: broken pipe"
These four network errors were discovered during the local reproduction of the
issue.

However, during a live run, a new transient network error "WebidentityErr:
failed to retrieve credentials ... status code: 408" was observed (Note the
status code 408 in particular). In order to update the retry logic to be more
robust against unanticipated transient errors, we relax the retry logic to retry
on all errors.

fix(actions): scope WatchForUpdates pub/sub by run to stop cross-run contamination

Watch subscriptions were keyed solely on the parent action name. Every run's
root action is named "a0", so subscribers["a0"] collected the watch channels
of every concurrent run, and notifySubscribers fanned each child update out to
all of them with no run filter. A parent therefore received child updates from
every other run watching "a0".

Combined with the SDK informer caching children by bare action name (and the
fanout example naming children deterministically, so names collide across runs),
a child that SUCCEEDED in one run had its cached phase repeatedly clobbered back
to RUNNING by another run's same-named child. The parent never observed all of
its own children simultaneously terminal and hung in Executing forever. Observed
on flyte-development under concurrent load: a parent pod's log referenced dozens
of foreign runs, with one child's phase oscillating RUNNING/SUCCEEDED.

Scope the subscription by (run, parent action): Subscribe/Unsubscribe now take a
run name and key on runName+"/"+parentActionName, and notifySubscribers routes
on the child update's own run. This isolates each run's watch stream at the
source.

refactor(dataproxy): keep GetCloudCredentials to the IDL, not an implementation

flyte2's dataproxy is not the process that serves DataProxyService in a Union
deployment, so an implementation here would never run there:

* a Union dataplane's dataproxy is the union image with `args: [dataproxy,
  serve]` (helm-charts charts/dataplane/templates/dataproxy/deployment.yaml);
* that binary registers the flyteidl2 service itself —
  `flyte2DataproxyConnect.NewDataProxyServiceHandler(NewFlyteDataProxyServerV2(...))`;
* and its handler embeds UnimplementedDataProxyServiceHandler with a comment
  saying that is precisely so the flyteidl2 interface can gain RPCs before
  their implementations land there.

So this PR keeps what every caller genuinely needs from the IDL — the RPC, its
messages and enums, and OPERATION_GET_CLOUD_CREDENTIALS for routing — and the
implementation moves to where it will actually execute. An OSS implementation
on flyte2's own service is still worth having for anyone running that binary,
but it is a separate change and should not gate this one.

Removes the AWS STS dependency along with it, so go.mod is untouched.

refactor(runs): store created_by subject, resolve identity at read

Reshape run attribution to match cloud's pattern (apps/workspace entities):
store the creator's OIDC subject as a queryable, indexed created_by TEXT column
instead of a serialized EnrichedIdentity blob, and resolve the display identity
(name/email) from the subject at read time.

Why:
- Filtering/listing by owner needs a queryable scalar; a BYTEA protobuf blob
  can't be indexed or WHERE-filtered (review feedback).
- Resolving name/email at read avoids staleness when a user renames in the IdP.

Changes:
- migration: actions.created_by TEXT + idx_actions_created_by (replaces the
  executed_by BYTEA column); created_by added to ActionColumnsSet (filterable).
- write: capture only the subject (subjectFromHeaders); drop the synchronous
  userinfo enrichment from CreateRun's hot path.
- read: actionMetadataFromModel resolves the subject to ActionMetadata.executed_by;
  the standalone service has no directory so it returns subject-only, deployments
  with an identity service (cloud) resolve name/email.
- remove the write-path userinfo enricher and the now-unused EmailHeader config
  (email is no longer captured at write).

feat(executor): stamp run, action, attempt and task-name labels on task pods

Task pods launched by the v2 executor only carried org/project/domain labels,
so per-pod metric series (DCGM, cAdvisor, kube-state-metrics) could not be
joined back to the run and action that produced them, and consumers had to
fall back to matching on pod names.

Inject four more labels in NewTaskExecutionMetadata, which plugin_manager's
addObjectMetadata already unions onto every object it builds:

  run        the run name
  action     the action name
  attempt    the 1-based attempt number
  task-name  the registered task name from the task template

The names are bare, matching the project/domain/organization labels already
injected, so kube-state-metrics surfaces them as label_run, label_action,
label_attempt and label_task_name, which is what the existing PromQL pod
filter expects. Values go through a new SanitizeLabelValue helper so task
names and run names that are not valid label values do not make the pod
unschedulable; a value that sanitizes to empty is left unstamped rather than
stamped blank.

artifact: record the parent version of an artifact version (#7955)

Artifact version history was implicitly linear: the only ordering between
versions of a name was creation time, so a version branched off an older
one was indistinguishable from one that continued the newest.

Add ArtifactSpec.parent_version — the version of the same artifact a
version was derived from. Only the version is carried, not a full
identifier: a parent is always another version of the same
org/project/domain/name, so the child's own identity already scopes it.
The reference is stored as given and never resolved; publication order is
not guaranteed, so a dangling parent is a tolerated state.

ProducedArtifact gains the same field so task-produced versions, which are
the common case, can declare their parent at registration; the backend
copies it verbatim into the spec.

ListArtifacts documents a parent_version EQUAL filter, which serves the
downward direction of lineage (the children of a version) that the stored
pointer alone cannot be followed in.

fix(config): serialize Duration as a flat string under YAML

config.Duration only implemented MarshalJSON, so gopkg.in/yaml.v2/v3 (which
does not honor MarshalJSON) serialized the embedded time.Duration as a nested
`duration:` map. Any config that serializes a Duration to YAML and is read
back through the viper/mapstructure config loader (TagName json +
StringToTimeDurationHookFunc, which expects a string like "30s") would fail
to decode.

This first surfaced with the connector keepalive config: the operator writes
the connector configmap with yaml.v2, emitting `time:\n  duration: 30s`,
which the connector plugin could not read back. Add MarshalYAML/UnmarshalYAML
so Duration round-trips as a flat "30s" string under YAML.

patch instead of update to clear finalizers (#881) (#7311)

During a recent issue w/ woven, we noticed the informer cache was off causing for pods to not have their finalizers cleared. There have been rare instances across customer clusters in which pods aren't able to terminate due to not having their finalizers cleared.

This change clears finalizers using Patch (merge patch) instead of Update as to reduce instances of stale state in the informer cache causing conflicts when updating the pod. Also adding a metric to track failures when clearing finalizers.

[BUG] use deep copy of bit arrays when getting array node state (#5681)

* [BUG] add retries to handle array node eventing race condition (#421)

If there is an error updating a [FlyteWorkflow CRD](https://github.com/unionai/flyte/blob/6a7207c5345604a28a9d4e3699becff767f520f5/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/handler.go#L378), then the propeller streak ends without the CRD getting updated and the in-memory copy of the FlyteWorkflow is not utilized on the next loop.

[TaskPhaseVersion](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/apis/flyteworkflow/v1alpha1/node_status.go#L239) is stored in the FlyteWorkflow. This is incremented when there is an update to node/subnode state to ensure that events are unique. If the events stay in the same state and have the same TaskPhaseVersion, then they [get short-circuited and don't get emitted to admin](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/events/admin_eventsink.go#L59) or will get returned as an [AlreadyExists error](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flyteadmin/pkg/manager/impl/task_execution_manager.go#L172) and get [handled in propeller to not bubble up in an error](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/nodes/node_exec_context.go#L38).

We can run into issues with ArrayNode eventing when:
- array node handler increments task phase version from "0" to "1"
- admin event sink emits event with version "1"
- the propeller controller is not able to update the FlyteWorkflow CRD, so the ArrayNodeStatus indicates taskPhaseVersion is still 0
- next loop, array node handler increments task phase version from "0" to "1"
- admin event sink prevents the event from getting emitted as an event with the same ID has already been received. No error is bubbled up.

This means we lose subnode state until there is an event that contains an update to that subnode. If the lost state is the subnode reaching a terminal state, then the subnode state (from admin/UI) is "stuck" in a non-terminal state.

I confirmed this to be an issue in the load-test-cluster. Whenever, there was an [error syncing the FlyteWorkflow](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/workers.go#L91), the next round of eventing in ArrayNode would fail unless the ArrayNode phase changed.

fix(connector): add gRPC keepalive and default UNAVAILABLE retry policy

Connector RPCs frequently traverse an L7 gateway (e.g. the Knative/Kourier
Envoy gateway) that reaps idle HTTP/2 connections and sends GOAWAY/drain on
routing changes. The cached *grpc.ClientConn then fails the next RPC with
"error reading server preface: ... use of closed network connection"
(gRPC code Unavailable), surfacing as 'failed to create task from connector'.

- Add client keepalive (Time=30s, Timeout=10s, PermitWithoutStream=true) so
  long-lived connector connections are not reaped while idle and dead
  connections are detected proactively.
- Introduce defaultGRPCServiceConfig (round-robin LB + retryPolicy on
  UNAVAILABLE + retryThrottling) and have getGrpcConnection fall back to it
  when a Deployment does not set DefaultServiceConfig, so every deployment
  (DefaultConnector, connectors, connectorApps) gets LB + retry uniformly
  without per-deployment config.

[Bug] Update resource failures w/ Finalizers set  (#423) (#5673)

## Overview
when [informer cache has stale values](https://github.com/unionai/flyte/blob/1e82352dd95f89630e333fe6105d5fdb5487a24e/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/nodes/task/k8s/plugin_manager.go#L478), we cannot update the k8s resource when [clearing finalizers](https://github.com/unionai/flyte/blob/1e82352dd95f89630e333fe6105d5fdb5487a24e/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/nodes/task/k8s/plugin_manager.go#L450) and get `Error: Operation cannot be fulfilled on pods.` The current implementation bubbles up the error resulting in a system retry. By the next loop, the informer cache is up to date and the update is able to be applied. However, in an ArrayNode with many subnodes getting executed in parallel, the execution can easily run out of retries.

This update adds a basic retry with exponential backoff to wait for the informer cache to get up to date.

## Test Plan
Ran in dogfood-gcp
- https://buildkite.com/unionai/managed-cluster-staging-sync/builds/4622 + manually updated configmap to enabled finalizers
- Run without change (https://dogfood-gcp.cloud-staging.union.ai/console/projects/flytesnacks/domains/development/executions/fd16ac81fd7b5480fb6f/nodes)
- Run with change (https://dogfood-gcp.cloud-staging.union.ai/console/projects/flytesnacks/domains/development/executions/f016a3be7fa304db5a77/nodeId/n0/nodes)
confirmed in logs that conflict errors:
```
{"json":{"exec_id":"f016a3be7fa304db5a77","node":"n0/n42","ns":"development","res_ver":"146129599","routine":"worker-66","src":"plugin_manager.go:455","wf":"flytesnacks:development:tests.flytekit.integration.map_task_issue.wf8"},"level":"warning","msg":"Failed to clear finalizers for Resource with name: development/f016a3be7fa304db5a77-n0-0-n42-0. Error: Operation cannot be fulfilled on pods \"f016a3be7fa304db5a77-n0-0-n42-0\": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again","ts":"2024-08-17T02:02:48Z"}

```
did not bubble up + confirmed finalizers were removed:

```
➜  ~ k get pods -n development f016a3be7fa304db5a77-n0-0-n42-0 -o json | grep -i final
INFO[0000] [0] Couldn't find a config file []. Relying on env vars and pflags.
```

[V2] Expand contextutils with org, service_name, cluster_id keys and logKeys (#7229)

* [V2] Expand contextutils with org, service_name, cluster_id keys and logKeys

The shared interceptor chain in Union Cloud sets context values using v1
contextutils.Key types, but v2 services (actions, leaseworker, leasor,
events-proxy, executorv2) use the v2 logger which reads v2 contextutils.Key.
Both are `type Key string` but are different Go types, so context.Value()
lookups fail silently and all context-propagated log fields are missing from
v2 service logs.

Add OrganizationKey, ServiceNameKey, and ClusterNameKey constants to v2
contextutils, and expand logKeys with ProjectKey, DomainKey, and the three
new keys so that GetLogFields() includes them in structured log output.

This is one half of the fix — the other half is a context bridge interceptor
in the cloud repo that copies v1 values onto v2 keys at request time.

Enabling lps with no outputs and adding error messages (#174)

## Overview
The PR fixes two issues:
(1) Enabling support for LPs without any output values
(2) Adding visibility into flytepropeller fetching outputs from URI.

There are two scenarios where we want to attempt to retrieve within FlytePropeller; namely when gRPC message size does not allow output literals to be sent and when flyteadmin sends only the outputURI (and no literals). Previously, the retry was performed automatically and the cause was lost. This PR adds a best effort attempt here, that will still surely break in some deployments (ex. cloud control plane offloading to outputURI not accessible by FlytePropeller), but will ensure a much more verbose and meaningful error message when it fails.

An example for gRPC message that exceeded capacity, FlyteConsole failure displays:`
```
`Last known status message: unable to retrieve output literals: [rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = grpc: received message larger than max (6400049 vs. 4194304)] <omitted mocked retrieval failure>
```

## Test Plan
Tested locally with the below workflow definitions (among others), but should ensure this works on cloud configuration on dogfood as well.

```
import typing
from flytekit import current_context, task, workflow, LaunchPlan, Resources

@task(requests=Resources(mem="8G", cpu="4"))
def build_int_list(count: int) -> typing.List[int]:
    x = []
    for i in range(count):
        x.append(0)
    return x

@workflow
def build_int_list_wf(count: int) -> typing.List[int]:
    return build_int_list(count=count)

build_int_list_lp = LaunchPlan.get_default_launch_plan(current_context(), build_int_list_wf)

@workflow
def my_wf(count: int) -> typing.List[int]:
    return build_int_list_lp(count=count)


@task
def hello_world():
    print("hello world")

@workflow
def hello_world_wf():
    hello_world()

hello_world_lp = LaunchPlan.get_default_launch_plan(current_context(), hello_world_wf)

@workflow
def my_wf_2():
    hello_world_lp()
```

stow v0.5.1 (flyteorg/stow#32): since v0.5.0, the S3 provider read each
body below 16 MiB fully into memory and allocated 48 MiB of part buffers up
front for larger ones, even for an *os.File. Seekable bodies are now
uploaded straight from the file: one PutObject below the threshold, and a
multipart upload of section readers above it.

This bounds the copilot uploader's memory per file regardless of file size,
complementing the concurrency cap from #8149.

* fix

* Give the system retry event a version the store can keep

Two defects the devbox found that the unit tests could not. Action events are
stored under (action, attempt, phase, version) and a duplicate key is dropped
on insert, so the retry event, which keeps its attempt and reports the Queued
phase the launch events already used, was discarded and the preemption stayed
invisible. It now takes its version from a range plugins never reach, under
the signed 32-bit ceiling the column imposes.

A failure to publish it no longer holds the attempt back either: the event
only explains the retry, and returning early on it left the action reconciling
the same dead pod forever.

refactor(devbox): keep the dashboard as JSON, not embedded in the manifest

The dashboard was 1,390 of monitoring.yaml's 1,615 lines — 86% of the file —
as an indented literal block inside a ConfigMap. It reviewed as an
unreadable blob and buried the 225 lines of manifest that people actually
need to read.

It now lives at monitoring/dashboards/flyte-v2.json and the ConfigMap is
built from the directory at apply time. Diffs render as JSON, and dropping
another .json in there is enough to add a dashboard — Grafana's file
provisioner picks up whatever is mounted.

Publishing to grafana.com was the alternative. Keeping it in-repo means a
metric rename and its dashboard update ride in the same PR and get reviewed
together, and the stack keeps working without reaching grafana.com at pod
start. The two are not exclusive if we later want it discoverable there.

Verified by deleting the ConfigMap and re-running `make monitoring`: it is
recreated from the file, Grafana rolls out, /d/oss/flyte-v2 returns 200, and
the dashboard still has 24 panels with both template variables.

refactor(gpufault): the fault relevance window lives with the contract (#7957)

* refactor(gpufault): the fault relevance window lives with the contract

Whether a fault was firing close enough to a failure to explain it is part of what
a GPU fault means, not a detail of how the executor reads events. Keeping it in
the executor meant the next consumer had to copy it, and one already has: the
leaseworker in unionai/cloud carries its own transcription of the same interval
arithmetic and the same two durations, which is two places to get the aggregated
event case wrong.

RelevantToFailure and the two durations it reads move into gpufault, which is
already the one definition of the fault contract. It takes plain times rather than
the executor's cached event type, so the package stays free of executor imports
and any consumer with a first-recorded and a last-observed time can ask the
question. The semantics are unchanged: a fault is active from when it was first
recorded until it was last seen, either time standing in for the other when one is
missing, and it explains a failure when that stretch overlaps the window before
the failure and the small slack after it.

The executor keeps its tests. They go through classifyGpuFailure rather than
calling the check directly, so they still earn their place: they are what catches
the executor handing the two times over in the wrong order, which the new
unit tests in gpufault cannot see.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Samhita Alla <aallasamhita@gmail.com>

* refactor(flytek8s): export the failure anchor a fault is judged against

Working out when a pod's trouble actually happened is the other half of deciding
whether a GPU fault explains a failure, and it was still private to the executor.
The leaseworker in unionai/cloud is now adopting the relevance check, so without
this it would carry a second copy that has to move in lockstep with the first.

PodFailureTime moves to flytek8s, which is where pod inspection already lives, and
lands next to GetLastTransitionOccurredAt on purpose: that function is the reason
this one exists. It reports the latest transition across every container including
the init containers, so for a pod that failed while its containers were still
running it hands back the time the container started. Anchoring a six-hour task on
its own start puts every real fault outside the window. PodFailureTime takes the
latest terminated main container instead, then the deletion timestamp an eviction
leaves behind, and only then whatever time the caller already had.

It stays out of gpufault, which has no Kubernetes imports and should keep none.
phaseInfoOccurredAt stays in the executor: it reads a PhaseInfo, not a pod, and
nothing outside the plugin machinery has one.

The table tests move with the function and gained the cases that were awkward to
reach through the executor, including one asserting the divergence from
GetLastTransitionOccurredAt that motivates the whole helper. The executor keeps
its end-to-end test for the evicted pod, which is what catches the anchor being
wired up wrong rather than computed wrong.

Let clients run the device flow against the OIDC provider and send ID tokens

flyteadmin's built-in authorization server has no device authorization
endpoint, so flytectl on a host without a browser has no way to log in as
a user. flyteadmin does accept OIDC ID tokens from its userAuth provider
over gRPC when they are sent with the IDToken scheme, the same path the
console uses. This change lets the Go admin client use that path:

- admin.deviceAuthorizationUrl (DeviceFlow) and admin.authorizationUrl
  (Pkce), each together with the existing admin.tokenUrl, run the flow
  against another authorization server, for example admin's userAuth
  OIDC provider. admin.clientId, admin.scopes and admin.audience are then
  used for the client registered there. Endpoints are configured
  explicitly, matching the existing tokenUrl override, so there is no
  discovery request and no new dependency.
- admin.tokenType selects the scheme sent to admin: Bearer (default) or
  IDToken. With IDToken the id_token from the token response replaces the
  access token for the device, PKCE, refresh and ExternalCommand paths.
  The token type is stored on the cached token so refreshes keep working.

Behaviour is unchanged unless the new settings are used. The deprecated
authorizationServerUrl key is left as is.

fix(executor): batch TaskAction event writes to unblock reconciles at scale

Under high held-action concurrency (tens of thousands of TaskActions), each
reconcile blocked ~2s on a synchronous per-event Record RPC that became a
single-row INSERT. This saturated the reconcile worker pool and starved
newly-created actions of a worker, so runs wedged under overload.

- Add eventBatcher: coalesces concurrent reconciles' ActionEvents into batched
  Record RPCs. Each caller still blocks until its batch commits, so delivery is
  unchanged (at-least-once); on error the reconcile requeues and re-emits,
  deduped server-side by ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING. Flush concurrency is bounded
  independently of reconcile fan-out.
- Make InsertEvents a single multi-row INSERT so a batch costs one commit
  instead of one per event.
- Skip the cache-hit Catalog.Get for already-RUNNING actions (a hit is moot
  mid-execution); the serializable-reservation heartbeat is preserved.

Measured on a 40k-held benchmark: per-reconcile event-write latency dropped from
~1980ms (p50) to <300ms with zero slow reconciles through the completion burst;
server-side inserts stayed <100ms.

gpufault: trust a pod's fault event only from its own node (#8153)

# Why

A GPU fault event is only worth believing when the fault emitter on the pod's own node wrote it. The emitter's credentials only let it record events for its own node, so an event reported from any other node did not come from the emitter watching the pod's GPUs. The executor's failure classifier checked the event reason and the regarding UID, but not the reporting node, and its event watcher did not record the reporting node at all. A consumer that wanted a typed fault for an attached pod event had to parse the free-text message, with none of these checks.

# What

- gpufault gains trust.go. FromPodEvent(PodEvent, Pod) returns the typed fault only for a trusted event: a GPUXidError or GPUSXidError reason, recorded against this very pod, and reported from the pod's node. The trade the classifier already made stays and is documented: when the pod is gone and only its name is left, the name match is accepted. A pod with a UID but no node was never scheduled and has no trusted faults. IsFaultReason is exported for callers that filter before logging.
- pluginsCore.ReasonInfo gains GpuFault, set only for an event that passed FromPodEvent.
- The executor's event watcher records the reporting node of each event: reportingInstance, else the deprecated source host.
- classifyGpuFailure uses FromPodEvent for its per-event checks, so a fault reported from another node no longer reclassifies a failure. RelevantToFailure still bounds the search in time.
- The executor sets ReasonInfo.GpuFault on the pod events it attaches to a phase, and toClusterEvents copies it onto ClusterEvent.gpu\_fault. The message is never parsed for a fault there.

# Tests

- New table in gpufault/trust\_test.go covering each rule and each trade, a wrong reason with a valid-looking message, and an SXid.
- plugin\_manager\_test: a fault reported from another node does not classify, and attached reasons carry a fault only when trusted. event\_watcher\_test: the reporting node is recorded and survives aggregation.
- go test -race passes for gpufault, pluginmachinery/core and executor/pkg/plugin/k8s, and the lint diff against main is clean. The new toClusterEvents spec is in the controller's Ginkgo suite, which needs envtest binaries and was not run locally.

A downstream consumer that tags faults on pod events switches to FromPodEvent once this lands.

Merge configuration.inline storage overrides into co-pilot's Secret

configuration.inline reaches the binary as 100-inline-config.yaml, which viper
merges over the chart's 003-storage.yaml. Co-pilot never sees that file, and
once a Secret is configured nothing travels on its command line either, so a
deployment that set its endpoint or session token through inline had co-pilot
talking to a different object store than the binary it belongs to.

read the file into secret_key by the time co-pilot's args are built. That
holds for the deployment's own config — it mutates storage.GetConfig().Stow

this file and never handed to a DataStore. There, dropping the path left
co-pilot with no credential at all.

Skip it only when secret_key is already set. Deployments that mount the
key file into their task pods keep the path they configured, and the case the
skip was added for still works.

Records what produced an artifact:

- external_ref: opaque reference into an external system
- unset oneof: manually created

feat(idl): typed gpu_fault on core.ExecutionError and workflow.ClusterEvent

Adds GpuFault to flyteidl2.core and an optional gpu_fault field on
ClusterEvent so a GPU fault (NVIDIA Xid or NVSwitch SXid) attributed to an
action attempt is carried as data next to the human-readable message: kind,
code, name, severity (user / warn / critical), the faulting device (GPU UUID,
host index, PCI bus id, node) and the blamed process when the driver named
one. The message is unchanged; the field is unset for every other cluster
event, so existing consumers are unaffected.

GpuFault lives in flyteidl2/core/execution.proto next to ExecutionError
because both the error and the cluster event have to carry it and core cannot
import workflow. core.ExecutionError gains gpu_fault = 8, set when a failure
was classified as caused by or coincident with a GPU fault, and
workflow.ErrorInfo gains code = 3 (the short failure code from the plugin's
ExecutionError, for example OOMKilled or GpuFallenOffBus, which the executor
used to drop) and gpu_fault = 4 mirroring the one on ExecutionError, so both
survive to the user without anyone parsing the message text.

A node-level agent that watches the kernel log emits these as
Kubernetes Events on the task pod from the node kernel log; the executor's
event watcher already forwards pod events into the attempt's cluster_events,
and this field lets the console and failure classification consume them
without parsing text.

Go, Python, TypeScript and Rust regenerated with the pinned buf 1.58.0.

```python
from flytekit import task, workflow, ImageSpec, Resources, dynamic

                       apt_packages=["git"])


@task(container_image=image_spec, enable_deck=True, requests=Resources(cpu="2", mem="2000Mi"))
def train():
    print("forward", flush=True)
    print("backwarddddf")


@dynamic(container_image=image_spec)

    print("dynamic", flush=True)
    train()


@workflow

    train()
    d1()
```

Adds appProtocol values of tcp on services

 * flyteadmin http port
 * flyteadmin grpc port
 * flyteconsole grpc port

   This is necessary because the ingress may be configured in a way that
   it sends TLS traffic to internal Flyte services. Istio will use port
   names to determine traffic - and may therefore assume the appProtocol
   of http, even though traffic from ingress -> flyteadmin is actually
   https. This misconfiguration prevents any traffic from flowing
   through the ingress to the service.

   Flyteadmin http and grcp ports *are* accessible using `http` and
   `grpc` values for appProtocol respectively within the cluster, but as
   soon as traffic travels between the ingress and the service those settings
   will not work. The most "compatible" setting is `tcp` which works for
   any network stream.

 - Adds the nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/service-upstream: "true"

fix(executor): enforce TaskMetadata.timeout as a per-attempt max runtime (#7910)

* fix(executor): enforce TaskMetadata.timeout as a per-attempt max runtime

The SDK already serializes max_runtime onto the TaskAction, but the
executor never read it, so hung tasks ran to success. Abort and finalize
the plugin at the deadline, emit TIMED_OUT, and retry only within the
existing attempt budget.

Closes #7901

Signed-off-by: shaon-chowdhury-euc <shaon.chowdhury@eucalyptus.vc>

* fix(executor): simplify max-runtime enforcement

Anchor the attempt clock on the plugin's reported start rather than
inferring it from PhaseHistory, ignoring reports that predate the
attempt. Collapse three deadline predicates into one, and persist the
resume marker before cleanup.

Fix DeepEqual on *metav1.Time, and resolve error info and fail rate
for TIMED_OUT actions.

Signed-off-by: shaon-chowdhury-euc <shaon.chowdhury@eucalyptus.vc>

* fix(runs): close the action watch stream only when the action itself is done

A timed-out attempt emits a terminal TIMED_OUT event for attempt N
before the action restarts as attempt N+1, and closing on attempt
terminality alone ended the WatchActionDetails stream mid-retry. Close
only when the action's phase is terminal and action_events has caught
up with it: the highest-numbered attempt is terminal and is the
action's current attempt.

Checked the other half of the concern too: the actions-table updater
already lists TIMED_OUT as a retryable phase, so the Queued row that
follows a mid-retry timeout is accepted — no stickiness to fix there.

[BUG] use deep copy of bit arrays when getting array node state (#5681)

* [BUG] add retries to handle array node eventing race condition (#421)

If there is an error updating a [FlyteWorkflow CRD](https://github.com/unionai/flyte/blob/6a7207c5345604a28a9d4e3699becff767f520f5/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/handler.go#L378), then the propeller streak ends without the CRD getting updated and the in-memory copy of the FlyteWorkflow is not utilized on the next loop.

[TaskPhaseVersion](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/apis/flyteworkflow/v1alpha1/node_status.go#L239) is stored in the FlyteWorkflow. This is incremented when there is an update to node/subnode state to ensure that events are unique. If the events stay in the same state and have the same TaskPhaseVersion, then they [get short-circuited and don't get emitted to admin](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/events/admin_eventsink.go#L59) or will get returned as an [AlreadyExists error](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flyteadmin/pkg/manager/impl/task_execution_manager.go#L172) and get [handled in propeller to not bubble up in an error](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/nodes/node_exec_context.go#L38).

We can run into issues with ArrayNode eventing when:
- array node handler increments task phase version from "0" to "1"
- admin event sink emits event with version "1"
- the propeller controller is not able to update the FlyteWorkflow CRD, so the ArrayNodeStatus indicates taskPhaseVersion is still 0
- next loop, array node handler increments task phase version from "0" to "1"
- admin event sink prevents the event from getting emitted as an event with the same ID has already been received. No error is bubbled up.

This means we lose subnode state until there is an event that contains an update to that subnode. If the lost state is the subnode reaching a terminal state, then the subnode state (from admin/UI) is "stuck" in a non-terminal state.

I confirmed this to be an issue in the load-test-cluster. Whenever, there was an [error syncing the FlyteWorkflow](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/workers.go#L91), the next round of eventing in ArrayNode would fail unless the ArrayNode phase changed.

Add ARCHIVED state to LaunchPlanState enum

Launch plan versions accumulate over time as each pyflyte register
creates new versions. This adds an ARCHIVED state (value=2) so old
versions can be marked and filtered out of list queries (e.g.
ne(state,2)) without conflating them with INACTIVE, which has meaning
in the active/inactive schedule lifecycle.

Archiving a launch plan disables any active schedule (same as
deactivate) but preserves the ability to launch executions from it.

Changes:
- flyteidl: Add ARCHIVED=2 to LaunchPlanState enum, regenerate bindings
- flyteadmin: Add archiveLaunchPlan handler in UpdateLaunchPlan switch
- flytectl: Repurpose --archive flag to set ARCHIVED state (was a
  deprecated alias for --deactivate)

Make the TaskAction requeue duration configurable

The controller requeued running TaskActions with a hardcoded 10s in eight
places, so the responsiveness of task actions could not be tuned and
neither could the reconcile load that comes with it.

Add executor config requeueDuration, following the same shape as
maxSystemFailures: a config field with a pflag tag, validation in
setup.go, a field on TaskActionReconciler, and an accessor that falls
back to TaskActionDefaultRequeueDuration when the field is unset. The
default is unchanged at 10s, so existing deployments behave exactly as
before.

The cache reservation heartbeat is tied to the same value. It was a const
aliased to the requeue duration, and it has to keep tracking it: a
reservation lease shorter than the gap until the next reconcile would let
another owner take the reservation while this TaskAction is still waiting.

devbox-bundled: drop security.insecure by switching preload to skopeo

The preload step ran rootless podman inside a RUN to fetch and save
image tarballs, which required `--security=insecure` and a daemon
configured with `--allow-insecure-entitlement security.insecure`.
Depot's hosted builders refuse that entitlement.

Skopeo does the same job (pull + retag + save as docker-archive) as
a privilege-free registry client, so the entitlement isn't needed
anywhere now. Drop it from the workflow steps and the local Makefile
builder config too.

skill, distributed via a plugin marketplace so users can install it with
  /plugin marketplace add flyteorg/flyte
  /plugin install flyte-deploy@flyte-skills

  .claude-plugin/marketplace.json
  plugins/flyte-deploy/.claude-plugin/plugin.json
  plugins/flyte-deploy/skills/flyte-deploy/SKILL.md
  plugins/flyte-deploy/README.md

feat(runs): populate RunDetails.executed_by from forwarded auth headers

Auth now terminates at the load balancer (ALB), which validates the request and
forwards the caller's identity to the runs service. Capture it at CreateRun and
surface it as ActionMetadata.executed_by so RunDetails records who ran a task —
previously always empty.

- identity.go: subjectFromHeaders reads the OIDC subject from X-Amzn-Oidc-Identity
  (ALB authenticate-oidc / cookie path) or, failing that, the `sub` claim of the
  forwarded Authorization: Bearer token (JWT-validation / SDK path). The LB already
  validated, so the token is decoded but not re-verified. subjectOnlyIdentity builds
  a minimal EnrichedIdentity (subject only), mirroring the cloud transformer fallback.
- DB: new nullable actions.created_by (VARCHAR(255)) storing the subject; written by
  CreateAction, read back into the model via SELECT *.
- CreateRun threads the subject into persistRunModel; actionMetadataFromModel maps
  created_by -> ActionMetadata.executed_by.

build: bump Go toolchain to 1.26.6 and patch grpc and go-toml

The released flyte-binary-v2 image reports 10 vulnerability findings under
JFrog Xray, 1 Critical and 9 High. Every one is a Go-ecosystem finding;
the Debian base contributes none.

Eight come from the Go toolchain the binary was compiled with, 1.26.5,
including CVE-2026-39821 at CVSS 9.6. The remaining two are
google.golang.org/grpc 1.83.0 and github.com/pelletier/go-toml/v2 2.2.4.
Each finding's fixed-version list names one of the versions used here.

The Dockerfile line is what determines the toolchain compiled into the
published image: the release job in flyte-binary-v2.yml builds through
docker/build-push-action with file: Dockerfile. The setup-go step in that
workflow feeds the lint and test job only.

1.26.6 rather than 1.25.13 because CVE-2026-46600 lists only [1.26.6] and
[1.27.0-rc.3] as fixed, so the 1.25 line would leave one finding open.

The go directive in go.mod is deliberately left at 1.26.5. It is a
minimum, so a 1.26.6 toolchain already satisfies it and stamps 1.26.6
into the binary. Raising it would force every consumer of this module to
move to 1.26.6 as well, which this change does not need.

fix(secret): invalidate cache even if the caller cancels

By the time invalidation runs the secret is already persisted, but the
caller's context was threaded straight into DNS resolution and the POSTs. A
client that hung up after the write therefore skipped invalidation entirely
and left the webhook serving the old value until the 24h TTL -- the write
succeeded, so nothing surfaced the problem.

Detach with context.WithoutCancel, which keeps values for logging and tracing
and drops only the cancellation, then re-impose the invalidation timeout so
the detached call stays bounded.

Also defer the Create and Update call sites, matching Delete. That does not
fix this bug -- a deferred call with a cancelled context fails the same way --
but it keeps invalidation reachable if an early return is ever added between
the write and the response.

fix(executor): ignore NotFound when GC deletes a TaskAction

GC lists every expired TaskAction (parents and children) at one snapshot and
deletes them individually. Child TaskActions have OwnerReferences to their
parent, so deleting a parent cascade-deletes its children; GC then reaches those
children in its list and the explicit Delete races with the cascade, returning
NotFound. That logged thousands of spurious ERROR lines even though the drain
succeeded. Treat NotFound as success (the object is already gone, which is the
goal).

```
import flytekit as fl
import time

THRESHOLD = 11

@fl.task
def detect_anomalies(data_point: int) -> bool:
    time.sleep(1)  # Simulate a time-consuming task
    return data_point > THRESHOLD

@fl.workflow
def map_workflow(data: list[int] = [10, 12, 11, 10, 13, 12, 100, 11, 12, 10]) -> list[bool]:
    # Use the map task to apply the anomaly detection function to each data point
    return fl.map_task(detect_anomalies, concurrency=2,)(data_point=data)
```

Rename LocalRunService to TracedRunService

The service records runs the platform does not orchestrate — work
executed on a laptop, in CI, or inside an agent framework, whose action
tree is reported here after the fact. 'Local' describes only one of those
callers and undersells the surface; 'traced' describes what the API
actually does.

Pure rename, no behaviour change:
  LocalRunService            -> TracedRunService
  CreateLocalRunRequest      -> CreateTracedRunRequest
  ReportLocalActionsRequest  -> ReportTracedActionsRequest
  ReportLocalActionsResponse -> ReportTracedActionsResponse
  LocalActionUpdate          -> TracedActionUpdate
  RunSource.RUN_SOURCE_LOCAL -> RUN_SOURCE_TRACED (tag 4 unchanged)
  Operation.OPERATION_LOCAL_RUN_DATA -> OPERATION_TRACED_RUN_DATA (tag 11)
  local_run_service.proto    -> traced_run_service.proto

Enum tags and field numbers are untouched, so this is wire-compatible;
it breaks source references only. Landing it now, before anything is
built against the name.

feat(secret): fan cache invalidation out to every webhook pod

Resolve the configured invalidation host and POST each address, rather than
issuing one request to the name. Against a headless Service the name yields an
A record per pod and Go's client picks one, so a single request would
invalidate one arbitrary replica and leave the rest serving stale secrets --
a failure that looks exactly like success. A ClusterIP Service or a bare host
resolves to one address, so both topologies share the path.

Chart now points cacheInvalidationURL at the headless Service; the Go default
stays localhost so local and devbox runs need no DNS.

Still best-effort: per-pod failures are logged with a count, and the write RPC
succeeds regardless.

fix: drop RunIdentifier.name pattern so ingest paths accept pre-existing run names

PR #7805 added DNS-1035 run-name enforcement in two places: a validateRunName
check at CreateRun (the only external ingress for user-supplied names) and a
buf.validate pattern on RunIdentifier.name. The proto pattern was intended as
documentation, but in deployments where protovalidate is wired it is enforced
on every message embedding RunIdentifier — including event reporting and
record/status replication. Runs created before the rule existed became
un-ingestable mid-run: their updates were rejected with InvalidArgument and
retried or dropped, leaving the runs looking stuck while pods kept executing.

Remove the pattern (back to min_len/max_len) and keep validateRunName as the
single enforcement point. New invalid names are still rejected at CreateRun;
identifiers on read/report paths accept whatever was already created.

perf(runs): don't block action writes on the NOTIFY pump

notifyActionUpdate and notifyRunUpdate did a blocking send on a 256-slot
channel from inside write RPCs, right after the row was already committed.
Once the pump fell behind, a best-effort wakeup turned into user-visible
write latency, and a cancelled request context discarded the notification
outright, leaving other watchers on a stale phase.

Replace the FIFO channels with a mutex-guarded pending set per notification
kind plus a capacity-1 signal channel. The writer inserts a key and nudges
the pump without ever blocking; the pump swaps the sets out and emits them.
Because a payload is an identity and every listener re-reads state from the
database when woken, repeated updates for one action collapse into a single
delivery, and memory is bounded by distinct pending actions rather than by
update volume.

A failed pg_notify merges its keys back into the pending set and retries with
backoff instead of dropping them, so a transient database problem costs a
delay rather than a lost wakeup. Two limits keep that retry from becoming a
new failure mode. A payload only spends its retry budget when the connection
was healthy and it failed anyway, which is what happens to a payload Postgres
will never accept, such as one of 8000 bytes or more; after enough of those
attempts it is dropped with an error. And a drain that delivered anything
resets the backoff, so one bad payload cannot slow every other watcher down.

A lost connection aborts the current drain so the remaining payloads do not
each trigger their own reconnect attempt.

Fixes #7757

fix(actions): tie an address to its attempt and pod; keep it across reconciles

From the review of #8201:

1. The executor's status write copied the whole status from the reconcile's
   read, erasing an address the actions service stored meanwhile.
   applyReconciledStatus keeps the address, which the actions service owns.
2. An address outlived the attempt or pod that reported it. It is now
   recorded with the reporting attempt and the TaskAction's SystemRetries,
   and AddressFromStatus delivers it only while both are current, so a retry
   or relaunch the controller starts hides it without the controller writing
   it. PutStatus ignores a report from an attempt older than the current one,
   and no longer moves Attempts back for one.
3. ActionAddress/PodAddress moved out of ErrorState's doc comment.
4. An empty ActionAddress withdraws the held one (documented); buf.validate
   rules on port (<= 65535) and url (a URI when set).
5. WORKER_KIND_MICROVM's comment states what schedulers that support it
   should do, rather than promising OSS behavior.

Also: the address docs (UpdateRequest, ActionUpdate, the CRD) match; the
CRD gains address.attempt and address.systemRetries (charts and devbox
manifests synced); a test for the watch snapshot path replaces the one that
could not fail; generated code from make buf in the CI image.

fix(helm): skip redoc when redoc.enabled is set to false

The flyte chart includes four templates: minio, postgres, redis, and redoc.
A property following the pattern `<template_name>.enabled` does exist in
the `values.yaml` file. It is used to enabled/disable the template.

Setting `redoc.enabled` to `false` does not disable the `redoc` deployment
and service. This changeset fixes that problem by following the same
approach with the other templates: wrapping the resoruces under the
`templates/redoc` with an `if` statetement evaluating `Values.redoc.enabled`.

feat(idl): typed gpu_fault on core.ExecutionError and workflow.ClusterEvent (#7878)

Adds GpuFault to flyteidl2.core and an optional gpu_fault field on
ClusterEvent so a GPU fault (NVIDIA Xid or NVSwitch SXid) attributed to an
action attempt is carried as data next to the human-readable message: kind,
code, name, severity (user / warn / critical), the faulting device (GPU UUID,
host index, PCI bus id, node) and the blamed process when the driver named
one. The message is unchanged; the field is unset for every other cluster
event, so existing consumers are unaffected.

GpuFault lives in flyteidl2/core/execution.proto next to ExecutionError
because both the error and the cluster event have to carry it and core cannot
import workflow. core.ExecutionError gains gpu_fault = 8, set when a failure
was classified as caused by or coincident with a GPU fault, and
workflow.ErrorInfo gains code = 3 (the short failure code from the plugin's
ExecutionError, for example OOMKilled or GpuFallenOffBus, which the executor
used to drop) and gpu_fault = 4 mirroring the one on ExecutionError, so both
survive to the user without anyone parsing the message text.

A node-level agent that watches the kernel log emits these as
Kubernetes Events on the task pod from the node kernel log; the executor's
event watcher already forwards pod events into the attempt's cluster_events,
and this field lets the console and failure classification consume them
without parsing text.

perf(events): use h2c multiplexing client for internal event hops

The executor->events-proxy and events-proxy->run-service hops were built with
http.DefaultClient (HTTP/1.1, MaxIdleConnsPerHost=2), which churns short-lived
connections under concurrent reconciles. Add app.InternalHTTPClient() (native
h2c via http.Transport.Protocols) and use it on both hops so concurrent RPCs
multiplex over a stable connection instead of re-dialing. Bench: 12x fewer
connection dials (2443 -> 200) at equal throughput; tighter p99.

fix(flytek8s): keep the specific code when a pod fails with a system error

DemystifyFailure worked out a failure code from the pod status reason and the
container states and then threw it away on the system path, reporting every system
error as Interrupted. A pod killed by a graceful node shutdown reached the user as
Interrupted whether the kubelet had said Shutdown, NodeShutdown, Terminated or
NodeAffinity, and that reason is the only record of what happened to the node.

The system path now reports the code it worked out. The two places that mean
Interrupted still say Interrupted: the SIGKILL branch sets it deliberately, and the
branch where the kubelet recorded nothing before the node went away now sets it
explicitly instead of relying on the return to overwrite UnknownError.

Nothing outside this function compares a failure code to Interrupted.

ci: publish npm package via trusted publishing (OIDC) (#7962)

* ci: publish npm package via trusted publishing (OIDC)

The TypeScript publish has failed for every tag since v2.0.17 — the
long-lived NPM_TOKEN secret can no longer publish (npm masks the
authorization failure as E404 "is not in this registry"), and npm is
deprecating 2FA-bypass tokens outright: they lose direct publishing
around January 2027 (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-08-npm-install-time-security-and-gat-bypass2fa-deprecation/).

Switch the workflow to npm trusted publishing: grant the job an OIDC
id-token, drop NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, and let npm exchange the workflow
identity for publish credentials (provenance comes for free). Also add
a workflow_dispatch input so tags whose tag-push run failed (v2.0.17
through v2.0.46) can be re-published once trusted publishing is
configured, starting with v2.0.46.

Requires a one-time npmjs.com change by an @flyteorg owner: package
settings for @flyteorg/flyteidl2 -> Publishing access -> add GitHub

feat(flytestdlib): add redis-backed storage to the storage module (#7501)

* feat(flytestdlib): add redis-backed storage to the storage module

Adds a "redis" storage type alongside the stow-backed and in-memory raw
stores, letting run metadata (inputs/outputs protobufs) live in Redis
instead of an object store. Objects are stored as plain Redis string
values keyed by the path portion of the DataReference
(redis://<addr>/<key>), with directories emulated as key prefixes via
SCAN. This path model matches the flyte-sdk redis plugin
(flyteorg/flyte-sdk#1191), so references written by one side resolve on
the other.

Selected with `storage: { type: redis, redis: { addr: host:port } }`;
username/password/db are optional. List is paginated by mapping the
storage Cursor onto the Redis SCAN cursor; ReadRaw enforces the
existing maxDownloadMBs limit; signed URLs are unsupported. Tests run
against miniredis (new test-only dependency) and cover raw IO round
trips, empty values, Head/Delete/List pagination, the download limit,
and end-to-end DataStore usage including reference construction and
CopyRaw.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ketan Umare <kumare3@users.noreply.github.com>

* feat(flytestdlib): route redis:// references via scheme when redis.addr is set

When storage is configured with a non-redis type plus redis.addr, wrap
the raw store in a scheme router: redis:// references dispatch to a
RedisStore, everything else to the configured store. This lets metadata
(inputs/outputs protobufs, via a redis:// metadata bucket prefix) live
in Redis while raw data, code-bundle signed URLs, and all other IO keep
using the blob store. Activated purely by the reference scheme - no
behavior change unless redis:// paths are used.

CopyRaw on the router reuses copyImpl pointed at the router itself, so
cross-backend copies (redis <-> blob store) work through plain
ReadRaw/WriteRaw.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Ketan Umare <kumare3@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(storage): address review feedback on the redis RawStore

- ReadRaw: enforce maxDownloadMBs via STRLEN before GET so the limit
  bounds the transfer/allocation instead of being checked after it.
- WriteRaw: honor the declared size — reject sizes over the 512 MiB
  redis value cap up front and bound the buffered read (LimitReader),
  erroring on streams that overrun their declared size.
- List: collect-sort-slice with an index cursor instead of exposing the
  SCAN cursor. SCAN's COUNT is a hint and its cursor cannot be rewound,
  so per-batch pagination either over-returns past maxItems or drops
  keys; full collection costs the same order (MATCH walks the keyspace
  anyway) and makes pages deterministic. Also allow listing from the
  container root (redis://<addr> with no key).
- Document that the configured redis.addr is authoritative and the
  reference host is advisory (the same server is legitimately reachable
  under different addresses from different vantage points), warn once
  on mismatch instead of rejecting.
- Doc/wording fixes in the package comment and signed-URL error; test
  hygiene: restore the global download limit via t.Cleanup.

Add artifact trigger automation: TYPE_ARTIFACT + ArtifactTrigger (#7749)

* Add artifact trigger automation: TYPE_ARTIFACT + ArtifactTrigger

Third TriggerAutomationSpec automation type: fire a run when a new version of
the named artifact is created. ArtifactTrigger carries the watched artifact
name, an optional exact-version pin, and the task input the artifact's value
binds to at fire time (mirroring Schedule.kickoff_time_input_arg). Also adds
RUN_SOURCE_ARTIFACT_TRIGGER so artifact-triggered runs carry their provenance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* First-class artifact info: Literal.artifact_id + Outputs.produced_artifacts (#7760)

Replaces the implicit metadata-key contract (magic "_ua"/"_uap" keys in
Literal.metadata carrying JSON payloads that SDKs and backends had to keep in
sync) with typed fields, split by lifecycle:

- core.ArtifactVersionId (ArtifactKey + version), core.ArtifactCard (hoisted
  from artifact.Card, same shape), and core.ArtifactInfo (description,
  user_metadata, card) — the descriptive payload shared by the production
  declaration and the stored spec, deliberately excluding identity so the two
  can never drift.
- core.Literal.artifact_id: the value's artifact identity, stamped once at
  registration and on artifact-bound inputs; travels with the value through
  every copy and participates in cache-key hashing by design.
- task.ProducedArtifact + Outputs.produced_artifacts: the transient
  registration declaration (output name, artifact name, optional version,
  info, declared type) — an action-scoped instruction that never enters the
  value stream. Field 3 on Outputs because outputs.pb blobs are sometimes
  cross-decoded as task.Inputs, where field 2 is context.
- artifact.ArtifactSpec now nests the descriptive payload as core.ArtifactInfo
  (value/type/source stay top-level); artifact.Card is removed in favor of
  core.ArtifactCard.

Run end2end tests on PRs (#136)

This is an initial release that enables End2end tests on any PR as well as merges to master. It's also possible for any fork to run the same CI steps.

This adds two additional github actions steps:
- Setup a [KinD](https://kind.sigs.k8s.io/) cluster (Kubernetes in Docker)
- Run `end2end_execute`:
   - Clone flyte repo master
   - Replace propeller image with git sha's image
   - Run `make end2end_execute` from flyte repo. This deploys `flyte` manifests and run `endtoend.yaml` pod and waits for all workflows to finish executing as expected.

Upgrade viper to v1.21.0 and fix case-sensitive key handling

Upgrade github.com/spf13/viper from v1.11.0 to v1.21.0 across all Go
modules. This required migrating from github.com/mitchellh/mapstructure
to github.com/go-viper/mapstructure/v2 (viper's new dependency) and
fixing two behavioral changes:

1. The sliceToMapHook now handles map[string]interface{} in addition to
   map[interface{}]interface{}, as newer YAML parsing returns the former.

2. Viper v1.21+ added insensitiveArray() which recursively lowercases
   keys inside arrays, breaking the array-based workaround for
   case-sensitive map keys. Added restoreCaseSensitiveArrayKeys() to
   re-read config files directly and restore original key casing within
   arrays.

Relates to https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/issues/5469

- go 1.21.5 was released on 12-5-2023 and go 1.21.8 was released on
   3-5-2024. During that time a number of high and critical vulns have
   been addressed

 - This PR changes the build process to float with the latest go release
   to automatically pick up remediated vulnerabilities rather than pin
   to a specific go release

 - Ideally there would be a renovate or dependabot process that
   automatically puts up PRs to this repo to update the pinning, which
   is safer from a build / test perspective.  Without that process in
   place, it's probably better to float with the latest patch release of
