fix(runs): bind a single-value VALUE_IN filter as an array (#8194)

ConvertProtoFilters passed a lone filter value through as a plain string,
but the VALUE_IN expression binds its argument with pq.Array, which only
builds a Postgres array from a slice. A VALUE_IN filter with one value on
a list request therefore failed with "pq: unable to convert string to
array" and came back as an internal error, while the same filter with two
values worked.

Keep the slice for VALUE_IN whatever its length. Other functions still
receive a single value unchanged.

fix(actions): scope WatchForUpdates pub/sub by run to stop cross-run contamination

Watch subscriptions were keyed solely on the parent action name. Every run's
root action is named "a0", so subscribers["a0"] collected the watch channels
of every concurrent run, and notifySubscribers fanned each child update out to
all of them with no run filter. A parent therefore received child updates from
every other run watching "a0".

Combined with the SDK informer caching children by bare action name (and the
fanout example naming children deterministically, so names collide across runs),
a child that SUCCEEDED in one run had its cached phase repeatedly clobbered back
to RUNNING by another run's same-named child. The parent never observed all of
its own children simultaneously terminal and hung in Executing forever. Observed
on flyte-development under concurrent load: a parent pod's log referenced dozens
of foreign runs, with one child's phase oscillating RUNNING/SUCCEEDED.

Scope the subscription by (run, parent action): Subscribe/Unsubscribe now take a
run name and key on runName+"/"+parentActionName, and notifySubscribers routes
on the child update's own run. This isolates each run's watch stream at the
source.

already a de-facto public contract — out-of-tree consumers reading plugin
state from storage (e.g. the dataproxy connector-log path in Union Cloud)
have to redeclare its shape locally just to decode it. Promoting the
struct + Phase enum from `pluginmachinery/internal/webapi` to the public
`pluginmachinery/webapi` package makes that contract explicit and lets
consumers import it directly.

- Drop the now-unnecessary self-import in `state.go` (ResourceMeta is a

  the public package.

ResourceMeta interface still decodes via the same separately-registered
wrapper types.

- taskaction.k8s.duration{op,error}: per-operation latency (get / update /

  otelconnect otherwise tags rpc_server_* metrics with net.peer.port (the client's

storage: bump stow to v0.5.0, pass the context to stow (#8115)

stow v0.5.0 moves its S3 provider to aws-sdk-go-v2, so the errors it
returns are smithy errors and no longer awserr.Error. The checks for a
missing bucket and for a bucket the caller already owns matched on
awserr.Error and would silently stop matching: a write to a missing
bucket would not create it, and creating an existing bucket would
become a hard error. Match on smithy.APIError and its error code.

stow v0.5.0 also adds functions that take a context. Call the stow
location, containers and items through them, so a request to the blob
store is cancelled with the context of the caller. The context of
ReadRaw now covers reading from the returned reader as well.

artifact: allow multiple parents for git-like merge lineage

ArtifactSpec.parent_artifact and ProducedArtifact.parent_artifact become
repeated parent_artifacts (same field numbers, max 32 entries). One entry
is plain derivation; several record a merge, making version history a
full DAG (git/Merkle style) instead of a forest of chains. Order is
preserved and the first entry is the primary parent; duplicates (after
scope/name inheritance) are rejected. Per-entry semantics are unchanged:
same org/project/domain only, empty key fields inherit the child's scope
and name, stored as given, dangling parents legal, immutable.

Also folds in the #7963 review feedback (previously #7964): buf.validate
max_len bounds on core.ArtifactKey fields (project/domain 64, name 255,
org 63, matching ArtifactName) and ArtifactVersionId.version (255).

Breaking IDL change to a field nothing consumes yet: the singular field
shipped in v2.0.47 days ago and has no users, so it is replaced in place
rather than deprecated.

The parent_name+parent_version children filter on ListArtifacts is
unchanged; it now matches artifacts having the given version among their
parents.

Idl/run spec resources (#8049)

## Why are the changes needed?

A run's task templates only carry the resources the author declared. Anything that schedules or accounts for those tasks before they become pods (Union's leasor) sees zero for an undeclared dimension, while the dataplane fills a platform default in when it builds the pod. The two disagree for every task that declares nothing.

The org/domain/project `task_resource` setting (`min` as default requests, `max` as a ceiling) is the intended source for those values, but nothing carries the resolved setting with the run. This adds it to `RunSpec` so every consumer of the run, control plane and dataplane, reads the same numbers.

## What changes were proposed in this pull request?

`DefaultSettings`, the run-scoped defaults wrapper from #8050, gains field 2, `task_resource_defaults`, of a new message. It is read as `RunSpec.default_settings.task_resource_defaults`:

```proto
message TaskResourceDefaults {
  repeated flyteidl2.core.Resources.ResourceEntry requests = 1;  // default request per dimension the task template leaves unset
  repeated flyteidl2.core.Resources.ResourceEntry max = 2;       // per-dimension ceiling on a task's requests and limits
}
```

A separate message rather than `flyteidl2.core.Resources` on purpose: `max` is a ceiling on both requests and limits, not a Kubernetes limit, and reusing `limits` for it would read wrong. The server resolves the field at run creation from the `task_resource` setting; a caller-supplied value is currently overwritten.

fix(executor): don't fail a gracefully-deleting pod as unexpected

checkResourcePhase reported any non-terminal object with a
DeletionTimestamp as UnexpectedObjectDeletion, a SYSTEM-retryable
failure. A pod under a graceful delete carries that timestamp and
stays non-terminal for its whole grace period, so the branch fired
continuously, not once.

That drove the controller to reset plugin state and recreate a pod
under the same name on every reconcile, colliding with the
still-terminating original (Create returning AlreadyExists) and
livelocking at API speed. MaxSystemFailures never bounded it because
the counter reset on the AlreadyExists-driven Queued transition every
lap.

Drop the branch and let the object be observed until it is actually
gone, at which point the existing NotFound handling above already
produces ResourceDeletedExternally.

The branch came from v1 propeller, where it caught pods that would
never finish deleting: a vanished kubelet leaves them Running with a
DeletionTimestamp, held by the flyte finalizer. v1 recovered by
starting a new attempt under a new pod name and clearing the old
pod's finalizer. v2 does neither, so the branch never recovered
anything here: if the object still exists, the same-name relaunch
livelocks (a stuck pod livelocks forever); if it is already gone,
the NotFound path reaches the same system retry one reconcile later.
Gating the branch on the deletion deadline would only postpone the
livelock to the stuck case. A pod stuck in deletion now waits for the
task timeout instead of looping.

Fixes #8066 (fix 1 of the proposed fixes; fixes 2-4 are hardening for
the quota/backoff and AlreadyExists/counter-reset symptoms and are not
included here).

fix: normalize msgpack Binary scalars for deterministic cache hashing

DictTransformer serializes dicts via msgpack which does not enforce key
ordering. Identical dicts with different key orderings produce different
byte sequences, leading to unexpected cache misses.

Add normalizeMsgpackBytes() in hashify() that unmarshals msgpack bytes
and re-marshals to JSON (which sorts map keys deterministically) before
hashing. This handles nested dicts and lists. If normalization fails,
the original bytes are used unchanged.

Closes #6776

Signed-off-by: Mitja Kleider <mitja.kleider@aleph-alpha.com>

* fix(copilot): let a raw container declare a permanent failure

A container's only channel for reporting its own failure is the error
file in its output directory, and Sidecar rewrote whatever it found there
as a RECOVERABLE OutputUploadFailed with no origin. A container that
knows its failure is deterministic could not say so, and a raw-container
task that exits non-zero instead is a system failure, spending the
cluster's system-failure budget rather than the task's retries.

Forward the document when the container wrote one, leaving copilot's own
upload failures classified as before.

feat(executor): correlate batched event writes with reconcile traces via span links

flush() runs on context.Background(), so batched Record RPCs surfaced as
orphan root spans, losing correlation with the reconciles that produced the
events. Parenting under any single caller would be wrong — a batch fans in
events from up to 400 different reconciles — so attach each contributor's
span context as a span LINK on a fan-in eventBatcher.flush span (deduped by
span ID; events.batch_size records the true count past the SDK link limit).
The otelconnect interceptor parents the Record RPC span under the flush span.
Noop until the executor tracer provider is registered.

still defaulted to type: datacatalog, causing DNS failures on every task
execution since the datacatalog service does not exist.

disabled, preventing connection attempts to a non-existent datacatalog
endpoint.

fix(runs): honor Offset in ListActions so WatchActions loads all child actions

ListActions only implemented keyset (CursorToken) pagination and silently
ignored the Offset field. WatchActions.listAndSendAllActions pages by Offset
(offset += pageSize), so every iteration ran the identical query and re-read the
same first page. Effects:
- only the first pageSize (100) actions ever entered the run-state tree, capping
  children_phase_counts at 100 regardless of the real child count (observed with
  a 10k-element map task).
- for runs with more than one page, len(batch) < pageSize was never true, so the
  initial-snapshot loop never returned and the live-update loop was never reached.

Add the OFFSET clause to ListActions when Offset > 0. Regression test asserts
offset shifts the page window and that walking by offset covers all actions and
terminates.

Added FastCheck Filters #minor (#100)

* Added FastCheck Filters

 - Fast check filters allow to look for existence of an item and
prioritize false negatives instead of false positives like Bloom filters
do.
False negative here refers to the filter returning a negative, even if
it is possible that the object was previously seen, instead of false for
an object that was never seen, as in the case of bloom filters.

The code had to be adapter from
https://github.com/jmhodges/opposite_of_a_bloom_filter/blob/master/go/oppobloom/oppobloom.go
because, the existing implementation had only one method that would
check and add. We prefer the case in which can check and then add as
2 separate invocations

fix(pytorch): propagate pod metadata to the PyTorchJob CR

BuildResource returned the PyTorchJob without an ObjectMeta, so pod-level
metadata (pod_template / k8s_pod labels and annotations) only reached the
replica pod templates via common.ToReplicaSpec and never the CR itself.
Execution-level labels were unaffected -- the plugin manager stamps those
on every resource in addObjectMetadata.

Set ObjectMeta from a fresh flytek8s.ToK8sPodSpec call, matching what the
ray and dask plugins already do. Deriving it from a replica spec would be
wrong: ToReplicaSpecWithOverrides builds a per-replica-group task context,
so group-specific labels would leak onto the CR.

Flyte-core define pod and container securityContext

 - Define secure defaults for all pod / container specs:

   * runAsNonRoot: true
   * capabilities:
       drop: ['ALL']
   * allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
   * seLinuxOptions:
       type: spc_t

   This is required in many locations where policy enforcement agents
   may be installed (like OPA Gatekeeper) which may otherwise prevent
   deployments from launching.

   The hard work of making sure the containers run as non-0 uids seems
   to have already been done given all containers are already specifying
   a runAsUser value of 1000 or 1001, so this should hopefully just be a
   little more hardening around restricting kernel permissions /

fix(copilot): download only a multipart blob's own parts

The downloader lists a multipart blob (a directory input) by its key, and
object stores list by raw key prefix: a listing of ".../index" also returns
a sibling such as ".../index_info.json". That sibling was downloaded into the
directory under a mangled name ("_info.json"), or failed the input download.

Items are now kept only when their key is under "<blob key>/". A listing
that leaves nothing is an error, as an empty listing already was.

fix(runs): key enricher cache by access-token hash, not token subject

The userinfo cache was keyed by the token's subject. Since that subject can be
shared across users (e.g. an OAuth client id — the very reason we resolve identity
via userinfo), one user's cached profile could be served for another user's run
within the TTL — cross-user identity confusion. Key the cache on sha256(accessToken)
instead, which uniquely identifies the bearer and is non-reversible. Adds a
regression test: two tokens sharing a token subject resolve to their own users.

feat: Apple Silicon accelerator for the devbox

A task or app that requests the APPLE_SILICON device class (`gpu="AppleSilicon"` in the SDK) runs
on the Metal GPU of the Mac a devbox runs on. A devbox container is a Linux VM with no Metal, so
the SDK hands the workload to a host-side bridge that `flyte start devbox --apple-silicon` runs;
the backend's part is to schedule it there and fail fast everywhere else.

- IDL: GPUAccelerator.DeviceClass APPLE_SILICON = 5 and GPUDevice APPLE_SILICON_GPU
  ("apple-silicon").
- flytek8s: for APPLE_SILICON, strip accelerator resources and GPU node affinity/tolerations and
  inject FLYTE_APPLE_SILICON_{ENDPOINT,WORKLOAD,TOKEN} plus OPENAI_BASE_URL/OPENAI_API_KEY, with a
  per-workload HMAC token (MintAppleSiliconToken) from the bridge secret. Without a bridge, fail with
  the non-retryable APPLE_SILICON_NOT_AVAILABLE, naming the host when the devbox reports it.
- Apps: the Knative app builder does the same; APPLE_SILICON_NOT_AVAILABLE maps to
  FailedPrecondition.
- Devbox: the bootstrap renders the bridge endpoint (host gateway IP), token secret and host
  platform from FLYTE_DEVBOX_APPLE_SILICON_* / FLYTE_DEVBOX_HOST_PLATFORM into the
  apple-silicon-bridge plugin config.

fix(cache): replace entries older than maxCacheAge on Put

With catalogCache.maxCacheAge set, Get treats an entry older than that
as a miss and the task runs again. The cache client's Put never sent

request sets overwrite or carries an expired max_age. It answered

every later run missed the cache again. Send max_age on Put and Update
when maxCacheAge is set.

fix(propeller): record events Admin already has in the dedup filter

The event sink only adds an event id to its dedup filter after a clean send.
When Admin answers AlreadyExists, the id is never recorded, so every re-emit of
that event passes the filter, takes a token from the sink's rate limiter and
makes a round trip that cannot succeed.

An execution that keeps re-emitting a recorded event can exhaust the limiter and
starve the other executions sharing it.

Record the id when Admin reports it already has the event, or that the entity is
already terminal. The error is still returned, so callers see what they saw
before.

Rename LocalRunService to TrackedRunService (#7763)

* Rename LocalRunService to TracedRunService

The service records runs the platform does not orchestrate — work
executed on a laptop, in CI, or inside an agent framework, whose action
tree is reported here after the fact. 'Local' describes only one of those
callers and undersells the surface; 'traced' describes what the API
actually does.

Pure rename, no behaviour change:
  LocalRunService            -> TracedRunService
  CreateLocalRunRequest      -> CreateTracedRunRequest
  ReportLocalActionsRequest  -> ReportTracedActionsRequest
  ReportLocalActionsResponse -> ReportTracedActionsResponse
  LocalActionUpdate          -> TracedActionUpdate
  RunSource.RUN_SOURCE_LOCAL -> RUN_SOURCE_TRACED (tag 4 unchanged)
  Operation.OPERATION_LOCAL_RUN_DATA -> OPERATION_TRACED_RUN_DATA (tag 11)
  local_run_service.proto    -> traced_run_service.proto

Enum tags and field numbers are untouched, so this is wire-compatible;
it breaks source references only. Landing it now, before anything is
built against the name.

feat(artifact): typed partitions on artifact versions

Partitions become part of an artifact's identity instead of free-form
labels: a version carries at most one time partition (with a key and a
granularity, now including WEEK) plus any number of string partitions,
and the set of keys is fixed per artifact name by its first version.

- core: Granularity.WEEK; TimePartition.key (defaults to "date"/"hour").
- artifact: ArtifactSpec.partitions and time_partition; ArtifactPartitionSchema,
  TimePartitionKey and PartitionSchemaMismatch; Artifact.partition_schema_mismatch,
  set by the service for a version whose keys do not match the schema. Such a
  version is stored and flagged, never rejected.
- artifact service: DeclareArtifact (fix the schema ahead of any version),
  GetArtifactSchema, ListPartitionValues; ListArtifactsRequest.latest_per_partition;
  "partition.<key>", "time_partition" and "schema_mismatch" filters and a
  "time_partition" sort key; ArtifactGroup.partition_schema,
  latest_time_partition and latest_partitions.
- task: ProducedArtifact.partitions / time_partition so a task publishing
  with produces_artifacts can name its partition; ArtifactTrigger.partitions
  (fire only for matching string partitions) and partition_input_args
  (bind a partition value of the triggering version to a task input).

Updates to README (#466)

refactor: move the Flyte v2 dashboard to repo-level monitoring/

The dashboard charts the rpc_* metrics any flyte2 emits, so it is not
devbox-specific — the same JSON is what you want on an AWS or GCP install.
Living under docker/devbox-bundled/ made it look like a devbox artifact and
buried it for anyone deploying elsewhere.

  monitoring/dashboards/flyte-v2.json    was docker/devbox-bundled/monitoring/
  monitoring/README.md                   how to use it in each case

The devbox manifests stay where they are: NodePort 30300, emptyDir storage and
a single static scrape target are devbox-shaped, and only the dashboard is
portable. `make devbox-monitoring` now builds its ConfigMap from
../../monitoring/dashboards/.

Move settings desc field option off extension number 50000

The desc field option on google.protobuf.FieldOptions sat at 50000, in
the range protobuf reserves for internal use within a single
organization. That range is only safe when you control every .proto
sharing a descriptor pool. flyteidl2 is published to buf.build, PyPI and
npm, so it routinely shares a pool with third-party protos, and desc
collided with another published extension claiming the same tag. The
collision fails extension registration at import time for anyone
importing both schemas.

Move desc to 1364, from a block of 1364-1373 requested for Flyte in the
protobuf global extension registry
(protocolbuffers/protobuf#29013). The block deliberately starts after
1314-1363, which is claimed by the currently open
protocolbuffers/protobuf#28919.

This is backwards compatible. desc is a descriptor-level annotation
living in FieldOptions, so it is never serialized into any RPC payload,
and every consumer references the generated symbol rather than the
literal number. The only fallout is transient and cosmetic: during
version skew, a mixed-version reader of a serialized FileDescriptorProto
drops the annotation as an unknown field.

Also correct the usage docblock, which referenced the org package and
org.E_Desc. The extension lives in flyteidl2.settings and generates as
settings.E_Desc.

fix(flytectl): print execution details holding a NaN

`flytectl get execution --details` extracts each node's input and output
literals into a map[string]interface{} and hands it to encoding/json, which
refuses non-finite floats. One task output that came out NaN - an eval
metric, say - therefore loses the entire detailed view of the execution, in
every output format:

    $ flytectl get execution -p p -d production my-exec -o json --details
    Error: json: unsupported value: NaN

Non-finite floats now extract as nil, so they print as null and the rest of
the view survives.

feat(gpufault): shared GPU fault contract and failure classification

A node-level agent can turn NVIDIA Xid and NVSwitch SXid lines from the kernel
log into a Kubernetes Warning Event on the task pod. Until now the message
format, the Xid name and severity tables and the parser had no home in this
repo, so an emitter and a consumer could only agree on them by copying, and
drift.

This adds flyteplugins/go/tasks/pluginmachinery/gpufault as the one definition:
the event message format (FormatEventMessage, ParseEventMessage, and Sentence for
the human half on its own), the Xid tables behind NameFor and SeverityFor, and the
conversions to and from the typed core.GpuFault, including FromEventMessage which
turns an arbitrary pod event into a fault or into nothing. The wire format is
unchanged, byte for byte, because events already recorded on running clusters have
to keep parsing.

On top of that it adds the classification the executor applies to a failed
attempt. CodeFor names the failure (GpuFallenOffBus, GpuEccUncorrectable,
GpuRowRemapPending, GpuNvlinkError, GpuGspError, GpuXidError) and ClassifyFailure
folds the faults observed on the pod into the failure the plugin reported: a
critical fault makes it a system retryable failure so it does not burn a user
retry on hardware the workload did not break, a user fault only names what went
wrong and leaves the plugin's verdict alone, and a warning rides along as data.
Every rule keeps the error URI, timestamp, worker, recoverability, task info and
phase version the original failure carried.

The package has no Kubernetes dependencies so both the emitter and the consumers
can import it.

fix(actions): never drop a child update from WatchForUpdates

notifySubscribers dropped an update whenever a parent's subscriber
channel was full. A dropped terminal update means the parent's SDK
informer never learns the child finished, and since it never re-lists,
the parent waits forever. Raising watchBufferSize only moves the
threshold: a 546-child parent still hung at 1000.

Each subscription now parks undelivered updates in a map keyed by child
action name, with a pump goroutine feeding the caller's channel. A newer
update for a still-parked child replaces the older one, so memory is
bounded by the number of children and nothing is dropped. The channel
returned by Subscribe is unchanged, so the service and mocks are too.

Closes #8104

artifact: allow multiple parents for git-like merge lineage (#7972)

* artifact: allow multiple parents for git-like merge lineage

ArtifactSpec.parent_artifact and ProducedArtifact.parent_artifact become
repeated parent_artifacts (same field numbers, max 32 entries). One entry
is plain derivation; several record a merge, making version history a
full DAG (git/Merkle style) instead of a forest of chains. Order is
preserved and the first entry is the primary parent; duplicates (after
scope/name inheritance) are rejected. Per-entry semantics are unchanged:
same org/project/domain only, empty key fields inherit the child's scope
and name, stored as given, dangling parents legal, immutable.

Also folds in the #7963 review feedback (previously #7964): buf.validate
max_len bounds on core.ArtifactKey fields (project/domain 64, name 255,
org 63, matching ArtifactName) and ArtifactVersionId.version (255).

Breaking IDL change to a field nothing consumes yet: the singular field
shipped in v2.0.47 days ago and has no users, so it is replaced in place
rather than deprecated.

The parent_name+parent_version children filter on ListArtifacts is
unchanged; it now matches artifacts having the given version among their
parents.

Cache image-pull-secret reads in webhook via controller-runtime informer

The embedded secret manager's mutating webhook issues two synchronous
kube-apiserver Gets per pod admission to resolve image pull secrets
(one against the reference namespace, one against the pod namespace
for the mirrored copy). At admission scale this is unnecessary load
on the API server.

Replace the bare controller-runtime client.New with a cache-backed
delegating client. The cache is started for the lifetime of the
webhook and watches Secrets cluster-wide; reads are served from the
informer, writes still go through the API server.

fix(flytectl): fall back to Docker Desktop socket paths when default is unavailable

On macOS with Docker Desktop, the Docker socket may not be at the
default /var/run/docker.sock path. Docker Desktop places it at
~/.docker/run/docker.sock or ~/Library/Containers/com.docker.docker/
Data/docker-cli.sock instead.

try well-known Docker Desktop socket paths before giving up. This fixes
`flytectl demo start` failing with "Cannot connect to the Docker daemon"
on macOS Docker Desktop installations.

fix(copilot): write the error document to the name the output reader reads

flytecopilot wrote its ErrorDocument to `errors.pb` while
RemoteFileOutputReader.IsError() looks for `error.pb` (ioutils.ErrorsSuffix).
Nothing read the file copilot wrote: the reader fell through to `outputs.pb`,
which does not exist, and the resulting Go error was classified as a system
failure. A transient blob-store error during output upload therefore burned
MaxSystemFailures attempts and died with MaxSystemFailuresExceeded naming a
missing outputs.pb, never consulting the task's own retry budget -- even though
copilot had already marked the failure RECOVERABLE.

- Default `--err-output-name` to `error.pb`.
- Have SidecarCommandArgs and DownloadCommandArgs pass
  `--err-output-name=ioutils.ErrorsSuffix` explicitly, so the two sides cannot
  drift again and a new propeller fixes an older copilot image too.

patch instead of update to clear finalizers (#881)

During a recent issue w/ woven, we noticed the informer cache was off causing for pods to not have their finalizers cleared. There have been rare instances across customer clusters in which pods aren't able to terminate due to not having their finalizers cleared.

This change clears finalizers using Patch (merge patch) instead of Update as to reduce instances of stale state in the informer cache causing conflicts when updating the pod. Also adding a metric to track failures when clearing finalizers.

fix(secrets): deliver flyte-native secrets to task pods

Secrets created via 'flyte create secret' were never delivered to task
pods. The secret service writes Kubernetes Secrets named
md5(EncodeSecretName(org, domain, project, name)) with the encoded ID as
the data key, but the pod webhook defaulted to the plain K8s injector,
which blindly references a Secret named md5(bare key) with the bare key
as data key - names the service never creates. Because the injected
env/volume sources are optional, pods started with nothing mounted and
failed later with opaque application errors instead of a clear 'secret
not found'.

Default the webhook to the embedded secret manager with the K8s fetcher,
which resolves secrets at admission using the same encoding as the
secret service, including scope fallback (project+domain -> domain ->
org) derived from task pod labels, and rejects the pod with a clear
error when the secret is missing. Align the flyte-binary chart so the
secret service and the webhook both use the release namespace.

Add an end-to-end naming-compatibility test: a Secret written by
CreateSecret at each scope must be found by the K8sSecretFetcher via the
webhook's scope-fallback lookup IDs.

fix(flyte-devbox): use relative redirect for console root route (#7914)

The root-to-console redirectRegex echoed back the scheme+host captured
from the request URL. Behind proxies that rewrite Host (e.g. GitHub
Codespaces forwarded addresses), Traefik sees http://localhost:30080/
and the browser is redirected there instead of the public URL.

Replace the whole matched URL with just the console base path so the
browser receives a relative redirect (Location: /v2) and resolves it
against the URL it actually requested. Works equally for direct access
and any proxy in front of the devbox.

fix(executor): match fault events by pod UID and last observation

Review follow-up on the classification scope. Identity now comes from the
event's regarding UID matched against the pod being classified, so a
recreated pod with a reused name cannot inherit its predecessor's faults;
the name-plus-window heuristic no longer carries that job. Recency comes
from the event's last observation: the watcher no longer ignores updates,
which is how Kubernetes delivers an aggregated recurring event, and stores
the freshest of eventTime, series.lastObservedTime and lastTimestamp without
touching the created/recorded watermarks other consumers advance on. The
relevance window now bounds only how long a quiescent fault stays relevant
to new failures on the same pod, evaluated against that last observation, so
a fault still recurring classifies while one that stopped long ago does not.

Refreshed entries are stored as new values rather than mutated in place;
list hands the pointers to readers outside the lock.

We also need to run a migration to insert labels that exist only in resolved_spec but are missing from the execution_tag table.

## Test Plan
1. Update workflow-exeuction-config. `flytectl update workflow-execution-config --attrFile wec.yaml`
```
domain: development                                                                                                                                                                                                                
project: flytesnacks
labels:

    a: b
    c: d
```
2. Run a workflow (The `execution.closure.resolved_spec` will have the label, but not in the `execution.labels`)
3. Rebuild the single binary with my changes
4. Run the flyte single binary and check if we insert the labels into the execution_tag table
5. Run a workflow and check the labels will be added to the execution_tag table.

staging -> canary -> production

Make the projected co-pilot config readable by non-root containers

DefaultMode 0400 leaves the projected file root-owned and owner-read-only,
and kubelet only widens group permissions when the pod sets fsGroup. Co-pilot
containers inherit the pod-level security context (pod_helper.go applies
DefaultPodSecurityContext to the podSpec, not just the primary container), so
any deployment running task pods as a non-root user got EACCES opening the
config and failed every co-pilot task at startup.

Verified on a cluster: at 0400 a uid-1000 container gets "Permission denied";
at 0444 it reads the file. The volume is mounted only into the co-pilot
containers, so being readable inside them withholds nothing 0400 would have.

requirements to Kubernetes ResourceList entries, ignoring the

from using alternative GPU resource types (e.g. amd.com/gpu,

Helm value.

  config.GetK8sPluginConfig() instead of using the ResourceNvidiaGPU
  constant directly.
- flytepropeller: convertTaskResourcesToRequirements now reads
  GpuResourceName from flytek8sConfig.GetK8sPluginConfig() instead of
  utils.ResourceNvidiaGPU.
- Update tests in both packages to assert against the config-driven key.

[V2] Fix trace issue (#7178)

* fix(runs): persist model CreatedAt in CreateAction for correct trace ordering

Trace actions set CreatedAt to the span's start_time so that parents
(which start before children but are recorded later) sort earlier in
ListActions ORDER BY created_at ASC. The INSERT was omitting created_at,
causing the DB to use CURRENT_TIMESTAMP (insert time) and reversing the
parent/child order — leading to "parent node not found" errors in
WatchActions when a child action was processed before its parent.

Non-trace actions leave CreatedAt as the zero value and fall back to
time.Now(), preserving existing behaviour.

Signed-off-by: Flyte-Bot <admin@flyte.org>

ci: publish npm package via trusted publishing (OIDC)

The TypeScript publish has failed for every tag since v2.0.17 — the
long-lived NPM_TOKEN secret can no longer publish (npm masks the
authorization failure as E404 "is not in this registry"), and npm is
deprecating 2FA-bypass tokens outright: they lose direct publishing
around January 2027 (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-08-npm-install-time-security-and-gat-bypass2fa-deprecation/).

Switch the workflow to npm trusted publishing: grant the job an OIDC
id-token, drop NODE_AUTH_TOKEN, and let npm exchange the workflow
identity for publish credentials (provenance comes for free). Also add
a workflow_dispatch input so tags whose tag-push run failed (v2.0.17
through v2.0.46) can be re-published once trusted publishing is
configured, starting with v2.0.46.

Requires a one-time npmjs.com change by an @flyteorg owner: package
settings for @flyteorg/flyteidl2 -> Publishing access -> add GitHub
Actions trusted publisher (repository flyteorg/flyte, workflow
publish-npm.yml). The NPM_TOKEN secret can be deleted afterwards.

fix(runs): close the action watch stream only when the action itself is done

A timed-out attempt emits a terminal TIMED_OUT event for attempt N
before the action restarts as attempt N+1, and closing on attempt
terminality alone ended the WatchActionDetails stream mid-retry. Close
only when the action's phase is terminal and action_events has caught
up with it: the highest-numbered attempt is terminal and is the
action's current attempt.

Checked the other half of the concern too: the actions-table updater
already lists TIMED_OUT as a retryable phase, so the Queued row that
follows a mid-retry timeout is accepted — no stickiness to fix there.

Exclude union reserved init containers in image builder mutation (#598)

## Overview
Unfortunately https://github.com/unionai/flyte/pull/596 broke secrets on serverless (where we have image builder enabled) because it began enforcing hostname replacement on union-generated init containers added to support the embedded secrets manager.

Instead of rolling that back and allowing custom images for all user defined image containers, I'd like to keep the additional security validation and instead exclude whitelisted containers only.

This poses a possible attack vector where someone could attempt to reverse engineer the union-generated secrets init container name I'm not quite sure how to get around, although this is made greatly more difficult by restricted user kubernetes cluster access in Serverless. One option: compare pod contents altogether to ensure the init container matches what we expect (a bit brittle to implement though because it requires moving the secrets manager init container code into a common location since we can't hardcode a pod spec in the config given all of our templatization 

I think the right thing to do is https://linear.app/unionai/issue/COR-2548/task-registration-validation-should-catch-reserved-container-names but I'll save that for a follow up to unblock secrets for now

Unfortunately this wasn't caught with automation due to https://linear.app/unionai/issue/PE-1610/run-api-tests-on-canary-and-internal-dataplanes-in-prod-for-managed

## Test Plan
Deploy to staging and verify I could run a basic secret workflow: https://serverless.staging.union.ai/org/katrinasvr24/projects/flytesnacks/domains/development/executions/alv5m5p4tbn2hfqbcvbd

```
@task(secret_requests=[Secret(key="my_secret")])
def fn() -> str:
    secret_value = current_context().secrets.get(key="my_secret")
    return secret_value


@workflow
def main() -> str:
    return fn()
```

Verified API tests here: https://buildkite.com/unionai/org-staging-sync/builds/3728#_

## Rollout Plan (if applicable)
Merge to main

feat(workflow): add ActionsService proto for action state APIs (#6899)

* feat(workflow): add ActionsService proto for action state APIs

Introduce a new flyteidl2/workflow/actions_service.proto that defines an
ActionsService consolidating state and queue functionality for actions.
Add RPCs to update and retrieve action state (UpdateActionStatus,
GetActionState), plus EnqueueAction, AbortQueuedAction, and Watch to
support queuing and observation. Define request/response messages for
UpdateActionStatus and GetActionState, including validation rules and
fields for action identifiers, attempt number, status, and serialized
NodeStatus state.

This centralizes action state/queue operations into a single service
intended to replace parts of the existing StateService and QueueService,
simplifies APIs for workers, and provides at-least-once semantics for
state watches.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* feat(proto): validate action attempt is greater than zero and regen pb

- Add buf.validate rule to require attempt > 0 for action request and
  response in actions_service.proto. This enforces that action
  attempts start from 1 and prevents zero-valued attempts from being
  accepted.
- Regenerate Go protobuf bindings (actions_service.pb.go) to reflect the
  added validation annotations and updated descriptor bytes.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* feat(actions): rename ActionsService RPCs and messages

Rename several RPCs and corresponding request/response messages to
simplify the ActionsService API and provide clearer, shorter names.

- Rename EnqueueAction -> Enqueue for queueing new actions.
- Rename Watch -> WatchForUpdates to clarify streaming semantics.
- Rename UpdateActionStatus -> Update and its request/response types to
  UpdateRequest/UpdateResponse.
- Rename GetActionState -> GetLatestState and its request/response types
  to GetLatestStateRequest/GetLatestStateResponse.
- Rename AbortQueuedAction -> Abort while keeping the original abort
  request/response payload types.
- Update comments to match the new names and keep deprecation notes.

These changes make the service surface more concise and consistent,
improving readability and aligning RPC names with their intent.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* feat(actions): extract ActionsService and add action RPC msgs

Move ActionsService into a dedicated flyteidl2.workflow.actions package and
adjust Go package path accordingly. Replace fully-qualified RPC types with
local message names for Enqueue, WatchForUpdates, and Abort RPCs to simplify
imports and proto usage.

Introduce new request/response messages for Enqueue:
- EnqueueRequest with action_id, optional parent_action_name, run_spec,
  input/run output paths, group, subject and a required oneof spec for
  Task/Trace/Condition actions.
- EnqueueResponse as an empty ack.

Add WatchForUpdatesRequest/WatchForUpdatesResponse messages to support
streaming updates with filtering by parent_action_id and payloads that
carry either ActionUpdate or ControlMessage.

Minor changes:
- Import flyteidl2/task/run.proto for RunSpec.
- Add buf.validate annotations and field constraints for required fields.

These changes centralize action-related APIs, improve type locality in the
proto, and prepare the ActionsService to replace previous StateService and
QueueService behaviors.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* feat(generated): add gRPC ActionsService stubs and servicer

Add generated gRPC Python bindings for the ActionsService into the
workflow actions package. This creates ActionsServiceStub with unary and
streaming RPC methods (Enqueue, GetLatestState, WatchForUpdates,
Update, Abort) wired to the protobuf serializers/deserializers, and an
ActionsServiceServicer skeleton that returns UNIMPLEMENTED for each
method.

These generated files provide the client and server class templates
required to implement and call the new ActionsService, which consolidates
state and execution management for actions (replacing previous StateService
and QueueService patterns). Keeping the generated stubs in tree enables
service integration and local development until the service implementations
are provided.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* chore(docker): bump Rust base image to 1.85.0

Update the Dockerfile build ARG for Rust from 1.84.0 to 1.85.0.
This brings the base Rust toolchain in line with the latest stable
patch release, addressing compatibility and security fixes in the
compiler and standard library. It ensures reproducible builds use the
newer toolchain without changing other language versions.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* refactor(actions): move actions proto package and go_package

Change the proto package from flyteidl2.workflow.actions to
flyteidl2.actions and update the Go package option accordingly.
This reduces unnecessary nesting, aligns the proto package with the
repository layout, and ensures generated Go code is placed under
gen/go/flyteidl2/actions rather than gen/go/flyteidl2/workflow/actions.
These changes simplify imports and reflect that the service belongs
to the actions domain instead of the workflow subpackage.

Signed-off-by: Sergey Vilgelm <sergey@union.ai>

* fix(actions): update grpc imports and service paths for ActionsService

Update generated gRPC Python stubs to reference the correct module path
and fully-qualified service names for ActionsService. Replace incorrect
imports and symbol names under flyteidl2.workflow.actions with the
canonical flyteidl2.actions module. Adjust all RPC method paths and
(de)serializers to use flyteidl2_dot_actions_dot_actions__service__pb2.

This fixes mismatches between generated stubs and the actual package
layout so gRPC clients and servers import the right protobuf symbols
and register the correct RPC endpoints.

Fix Docker build for CGO-dependent sqlite3 package (#7014)

* Fix Docker build for CGO-dependent sqlite3 package

The build was failing because `go-sqlite3` requires CGO, but the
Dockerfile used cross-compilation (`--platform=${BUILDPLATFORM}`) which
disables CGO. Additionally, the .dockerignore negation pattern for
`gen/go` was unreliable when the parent `gen/` directory was excluded.

- Remove cross-compilation, enable CGO_ENABLED=1 for native build
- Copy only gen/go instead of full gen directory
- Replace .dockerignore negation with explicit subdirectory exclusions

Move CacheMetadata from workflow to common/cache.proto

CacheMetadata is shared vocabulary: today it is embedded in ActionEvent and
ActionAttempt, and the eventual plan is a first-class CachedOutput.cache_metadata
field in cacheservice.proto once provenance stops being carried as an opaque
serialized value. From workflow/run_definition.proto that future import would
drag the entire workflow API closure into every cacheservice client; from
common — a pure dependency sink that imports no domain packages — it can never
create a cycle and adds no new dependency edges.

The message keeps its field numbers, so the wire format is unchanged; only the
fully-qualified type name moves (flyteidl2.workflow.CacheMetadata ->
flyteidl2.common.CacheMetadata), which proto wire encoding does not capture.
It gets its own cache.proto rather than joining identifier.proto, keeping that
file a pure identifier catalog per the package's file-per-topic convention.

refactor: align JobSet naming with upstream GeneratedNameMaxLength mechanism

The plugin manager now stamps object names via GetGeneratedNameWith(0,
GeneratedNameMaxLength) on both the create and lookup paths, so the clustered
plugin no longer needs to name the JobSet itself:

- Drop the name from BuildIdentityResource; the manager owns naming.
- BuildResource derives the same name only for the pod subdomain, which must
  equal the JobSet name for pod DNS to resolve.
- Delete buildJobSetName/toDNS1035Label; the DNS-1035 sanitization moves to a
  shared ConvertToDNS1035LabelCompatibleString util applied inside the
  executor's GetGeneratedNameWith, since FixedLengthUniqueID passes short
  names through verbatim and action names aren't constrained to label-safe
  form (dots / leading digits would be rejected by the JobSet webhook).
- Keep the replicas cap and the GeneratedNameMaxLength property bound
  (63 minus the worst-case JobSet pod-name suffix).

fix(copilot): let a raw container declare a permanent failure

A container's only channel for reporting its own failure is the error
file in its output directory, and Sidecar rewrote whatever it found there
as a RECOVERABLE OutputUploadFailed with no origin. A container that
knows its failure is deterministic could not say so, and a raw-container
task that exits non-zero instead is a system failure, spending the
cluster's system-failure budget rather than the task's retries.

Forward the document when the container wrote one, leaving copilot's own
upload failures classified as before.

Artfs2/lineage (#4681)

Changes for tracking artifact usage upon execution start.

#### Tracking tag
Before create, the artifact service should write a string under the `_ua` key in the form
```
project/domain/name@version
```
where the version is the version of the artifact to be saved.  At execution start, these tags are converted locally into artifact IDs containing only the artifactkey and the version (any partition information is not filled in).  These IDs are then emitted alongside any artifact IDs that were the result of artifact queries, in the `CloudEventExecutionStart` event.

The field in the idl has been renamed from `artifact_keys` to `artifact_trackers` to be less confusing.

#### Other changes
Remove an unecessary variable in registry.go file
Remove the initialization sql pattern in stdlib
Remove errant replace in stdlib go.mod

fix(plugins/ray): honor RECOVERABLE error.pb so Ray tasks retry

When a RayJob fails, GetTaskPhase reports a terminal failure regardless of the
task's error.pb. The k8s plugin manager only reads error.pb (and honors its
RECOVERABLE kind) when a plugin reports PhaseSuccess, so a failed RayJob never
gets that treatment: a user raising FlyteRecoverableException is reported as a
terminal USER error and the task's retries never fire, unlike container/pod
tasks.

Read the error file in the failed branch and map a RECOVERABLE error to a
retryable failure, falling back to terminal when the file is absent or
unreadable.

Scoop update for datacatalog version v0.2.38

feat(ray,kfoperators,clustered): name the child pods of a distributed task

The Ray, Kubeflow and clustered plugins track a CRD, so they implement
ChildPodDiscovery to tell the framework where the pods that actually ran the task
are.

All three build the same selector: the attempt's own labels, which the pod
templates they hand the operator already carry, narrowed by one label the
operator applies to the pods themselves. For Kubeflow that is
training.kubeflow.org/job-name, which is the CR's own name and so is known from
the moment the resource exists; one implementation in common covers PyTorchJob,
MPIJob and TFJob, because all three get their replica pods from the same
operator. For the clustered plugin it is jobset.sigs.k8s.io/jobset-name, exported
by the vendored JobSet API the plugin already imports. For Ray it is
ray.io/cluster, which KubeRay stamps on head and worker pods and overwrites on
the template, and whose value is only knowable from the RayJob's status because
KubeRay appends a random suffix to the cluster name.

Until that status is reported Ray falls back to the attempt labels alone. That is
not a wider search in any sense that matters, since run, action and attempt
already pin the selector to one attempt of one action; the most it can add is the
job submitter pod, which has no GPU and so no faults to contribute. The
alternative, declining until the operator catches up, would lose the fault on
exactly the runs where the cluster never came up healthy.

Ray also has to stop a task from taking its own pods out of reach. The head and
worker templates let a task supply k8s_pod metadata, and that metadata was
unioned after the execution labels with only the managed label re-forced
afterwards, so a user label named run, action or attempt would overwrite the
identity the selector looks a pod up by. All three templates now re-apply
flytek8s.PreservedPodLabels last, which is the same key set the selector is built
from. Dask and Spark are left for a follow-up.

The conformance tests are the point of the test additions. Each asserts that the
labels the plugin puts on the pod templates satisfy the selector the same plugin
hands the framework, for every replica type it builds. The two halves live far
apart and drift on either one would leave a GPU fault on a worker silently
unclassified, which is the failure mode this whole path exists to prevent.

fix(devbox): drop dangling GRAFANA_NODE_PORT references

The review removed the GRAFANA_NODE_PORT variable in favour of literal ports
(matching the other --publish entries), but three references survived in the
reachability check. With the variable undefined they expanded to nothing:

    if docker port flyte-devbox | grep -q "^/tcp"; then
        echo "Grafana:  http://localhost:/d/oss/flyte-v2"

so the grep never matched and `make monitoring` always claimed the port was
unpublished, printing a malformed URL — on a correctly configured devbox too.

Uses the literal 30300, consistent with how the port is published.

fix: prevent os.RemoveAll on empty path and add missing transaction rollbacks

Three safety fixes:

1. flytectl/cmd/compile/compile.go: Guard os.RemoveAll(tmpDir) with a
   non-empty check. When GetSerializeOutputFiles fails, tmpDir is ""
   and os.RemoveAll("") removes the current working directory.

2. flyteadmin/pkg/repositories/gormimpl/launch_plan_repo.go: Add
   defer tx.Rollback() after Begin(). If Commit() fails, the
   transaction is left open. Rollback after successful commit is a
   no-op, so this is safe and idiomatic.

3. flyteadmin/pkg/repositories/config/seed_data.go: Same pattern —
   add defer tx.Rollback() to ensure cleanup on any error path.

Adding basic authentication to Admin client (#31)

This adds the ability for the canonical golang gRPC Flyte Admin client to authenticate against an IDP.  This client is used by the execution plane (Flyte Propeller) when talking to the control plane (Admin) when it needs to send events primarily, among others.

The go-oidc library is used to discover the correct token endpoint necessary to retrieve a token.  Using the client id and secret provided from the configuration, a `TokenSource` is made and a `PerRPCCredentials` object is made from that which will keep request a token from the IDP if nil, keep track of expiration, and send the token along with gRPC requests as a metadata field when making calls.

Parsing ExecutionEnvID from Labels before taskID (#584)

## Overview
This PR parses the project / domain used to create the fasttask ExecutionEnvID from the Pod labels before the taskID. This is necessary in scenarios where the execution metadata differs from the registered task metadata, for example a workflow executed in domain "production" that uses a reference LP to access an workflow in domain "staging".

Previous to this change, we would create an ExecutionEnvID with the taskID metadata and then detect an orphaned environment based on the labels from the execution metadata. These competing execution envs would cause premature replica deletion on TTL.

## Test Plan
Tested and validated using reference LPs an actors.

set correct externalID in external resource (#684)

## Overview
Utilization details aren't available for array node subnode retries. The usage server grabs the external id on the task_execution event to get the podName. ExternalID's are set incorrectly on retry attempts since we use

```
	uniqueID, err := encoding.FixedLengthUniqueIDForParts(task.IDMaxLength, []string{nCtx.NodeExecutionMetadata().GetOwnerID().Name, currentNodeUniqueID, strconv.Itoa(int(retryAttempt))})
```
retryAttempt (of the subnode) instead of the parent array node's current attempt

ie on a pod's 2nd retry attempt of a subnode, and the first attempt of the parent arrayNode, the externalId would be:
exec-name-n0-2-n0-2 instead of exec-name-n0-0-n0-2, which would map to the correct pod name

refactor(actions): remove GetLatestState RPC and UpdateRequest.state

GetLatestState and UpdateRequest.state were placeholders for a JSON-blob
state persistence model that has since been replaced by PluginStateService.
With all callers on the new path, the RPC has been retired and the field
has been silently ignored — this drops the dead surface from the proto and
from the actions service implementation.

- Remove GetLatestState RPC, GetLatestStateRequest, GetLatestStateResponse.
- Reserve UpdateRequest field 4 (formerly `state`) to prevent tag reuse.
- Drop GetState from ActionsClientInterface and rename PutState to PutStatus
  with the stateJSON parameter removed.
- Regenerate Go/Python/Rust/TS bindings and mocks.

feat(copilot): preserve nested subdirectories in multipart blob uploads (#7490)

Uploader.handleBlobType built each file's storage key from info.Name()
(basename only) and skipped directories with a warning. Files written into
subdirectories of a Dir/MULTIPART output were therefore flattened to their
basename on upload — and because uploads run as concurrent futures, two files
sharing a basename across different subdirs (e.g. a/dup.txt and b/dup.txt)
would nondeterministically overwrite each other, silently losing data.

Walk into directories and key each file by its relative path from the blob
root (filepath.Rel + ConstructReference with the path segments), mirroring the
download side, which already reconstructs nested keys. Top-level files are
unaffected — their relative path is just the basename, so keys are unchanged.

Add an upload-multipart-nested test covering a root file, nested files, and a
cross-subdir basename collision.

Move settings desc field option off extension number 50000 (#7776)

The desc field option on google.protobuf.FieldOptions sat at 50000, in
the range protobuf reserves for internal use within a single
organization. That range is only safe when you control every .proto
sharing a descriptor pool. flyteidl2 is published to buf.build, PyPI and
npm, so it routinely shares a pool with third-party protos, and desc
collided with another published extension claiming the same tag. The
collision fails extension registration at import time for anyone
importing both schemas.

Move desc to 1364, from a block of 1364-1373 requested for Flyte in the
protobuf global extension registry
(protocolbuffers/protobuf#29013). The block deliberately starts after
1314-1363, which is claimed by the currently open
protocolbuffers/protobuf#28919.

This is backwards compatible. desc is a descriptor-level annotation
living in FieldOptions, so it is never serialized into any RPC payload,
and every consumer references the generated symbol rather than the
literal number. The only fallout is transient and cosmetic: during
version skew, a mixed-version reader of a serialized FileDescriptorProto
drops the annotation as an unknown field.

Also correct the usage docblock, which referenced the org package and
org.E_Desc. The extension lives in flyteidl2.settings and generates as
settings.E_Desc.

feat(runs): accept a "search" ListRuns filter matching run name or task name (#8035)

* runs: accept a "search" ListRuns filter matching run name or task name

The console's Runs page search box sends a single `task_name CONTAINS`
filter, so searching by run ID never worked. The Filter proto has no OR and
ListRuns ANDs every filter, so the console cannot express "run name OR task
name" on its own.

Add a synthetic "search" filter field, resolved by the run service before
the generic column allow-list conversion sees the request:

  search CONTAINS_CASE_INSENSITIVE x -> (LOWER(run_name) LIKE LOWER('%x%')) OR (LOWER(task_name) LIKE LOWER('%x%'))
  search CONTAINS x                  -> (run_name LIKE '%x%') OR (task_name LIKE '%x%')
  search EQUAL x                     -> (run_name = x) OR (task_name = x)

Any other function, or a missing, empty or multi-value term, is an
InvalidArgument. No IDL change: Filter.field is a free-form string validated
server-side. The Union cloud run service accepts the same field, so one
console request works against both backends; the console change follows
separately and must ship after this.

WatchGroups is left alone: the OSS grouped view does not consume request
filters at all.

OAuth2 (#8)

This adds OAuth2 support for Flyte Admin.

* Most of the logic has been implemented in the auth package.  Care was taken, at least attepted, to separate logic that exclusively dealt with oauth into this package.
* The code implements the authorization code flow, which means you'll need a client secret, and there is no implicit flow.
* Most of the core logic is in the `handlers.go` file, which has functions that create handlers (both HTTP and gRPC) that can be attached to existing servers.  See the `serve.go` file to see usage.
* Encrypted cookies are used to store the user's access (oidc) and refresh tokens.  Two other cookies (the CSRF token and the final redirect page) are stored unencypted.
 * Reworked some of the options handling around the base server logic in `serve.go`, specifically around SSL handling.

Docs forthcoming in the main flyte repo.  Also more unit tests and metrics here in another PR after the remaining auth work is done.

fix: drop the task entrypoint from the spark driver/executor pod template

Spark adopts a container from the pod template and writes its own driver
arguments onto it, but leaves command alone, because it expects the
image entrypoint to consume them. The template Flyte sends carries the
task entrypoint in command, so the kubelet ends up running

  a0 <task args> driver --properties-file /opt/spark/conf/spark.properties
    --class org.apache.spark.deploy.PythonRunner ...

and the task CLI rejects Spark's flags with

  Error: No such option '--properties-file'

preceded by the image entrypoint's "Non-spark-on-k8s command provided,
proceeding in pass-through mode". Every spark task fails this way on
clusters where the pod template path is active.

Clear command and args on the template's task container. The arguments
still reach the application through spec.arguments, which is how
spark-submit has always passed them; only the container-level copy goes.
Sidecars keep theirs -- Spark leaves every other container alone.

feat(idl): add TaskTemplate.worker_kind

The kind of worker that runs a task, as an enum. The scheduler sends a
task only to workers of its kind and holds it while none has room;
unspecified is the default worker that runs containers and plugin tasks.
WORKER_KIND_SANDBOX runs flyte.sandbox.orchestrator source in an
interpreter, with no container.

Routing on the task type string alone cannot tell a type the default
worker runs from one only a specialised worker can run, so it depended on
which workers were connected: when the specialised worker restarted, its
tasks went to the default worker and failed.

fix(k8s): stop custom pod-spec merge from diluting required node-affinity (Ray + Spark) (#7548)

* fix(ray): apply interruptible scheduling to Ray head and worker pods

Ray head/worker pod templates re-applied GPU node selectors after the
custom k8s_pod merge but never re-applied interruptible scheduling. The
merge (mergo WithAppendSlice) appends a custom pod's node selector terms
as new OR'd terms, so the (Non)InterruptibleNodeSelectorRequirement
seeded by ToK8sPodSpec only landed on the base term. A non-interruptible
task whose worker carried its own affinity could therefore still be
scheduled onto a spot node.

Add an idempotent flytek8s.ApplyInterruptibleScheduling helper that
re-applies the (non)interruptible node-affinity requirement to every
node selector term plus the interruptible node selector and tolerations,
and call it post-merge in buildHeadPodTemplate / buildWorkerPodTemplate
(mirroring the existing GPU re-apply). Head and worker both follow the
task's interruptible flag.

Adds TestBuildResourceRayInterruptible (head + worker, both flag values,
with exactly-once idempotency assertions) and the OR-hole regression
TestBuildResourceRayInterruptibleCustomAffinity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(ray): generalize post-merge scheduling re-apply to cover DefaultAffinity

Rename ApplyInterruptibleScheduling to ApplyPlatformSchedulingConstraints and
broaden it to also re-add the configured DefaultAffinity required node-affinity
requirements to every node selector term, not just the (non)interruptible
requirement. Same OR-append dilution: a custom head/worker k8s_pod whose affinity
is appended as a new term would otherwise escape the cluster's default-affinity
constraint (relevant on non-dedicated clusters).

Adds TestBuildResourceRayDefaultAffinityDilution, which reproduces the dilution
(appended custom term missing the default-affinity requirement) and passes with
the generalized re-apply.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(spark): apply platform scheduling after custom driver/executor pod merge

createDriverSpec/createExecutorSpec merge the custom driver/executor k8s_pod onto
the base pod (MergeOverlayPodSpecOntoBase) but re-applied no scheduling afterward,
unlike Ray. A driver/executor whose custom pod carries its own node-affinity term
therefore lost the default-affinity and (non)interruptible requirements via the
same OR-append dilution, e.g. an executor under interruptible=false could still be
scheduled on a spot node.

Call flytek8s.ApplyPlatformSchedulingConstraints after each merge (driver forced
non-interruptible, executor following the task flag). Idempotent, so the no-custom-
pod path is unchanged.

Adds TestBuildResourceSparkExecutorAffinityDilution reproducing the executor
dilution.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Explain why dropping secret_key_path is safe

The comment justified skipping the flag but not why co-pilot still ends up
with a credential, which makes the skip read like it strands accesskey
deployments with nothing.

It does not: newStowRawStore resolves secret_key_path into secret_key in the
very map this loop iterates, because it mutates storage.GetConfig().Stow.Config
in place, and the executor hands it that global config at startup. By the time
co-pilot's args are built the resolved credential is already under secret_key,
so only the unusable path is dropped.

Upgrade viper to v1.21.0 and fix case-sensitive key handling (#7013)

Upgrade github.com/spf13/viper from v1.11.0 to v1.21.0 across all Go
modules. This required migrating from github.com/mitchellh/mapstructure
to github.com/go-viper/mapstructure/v2 (viper's new dependency) and
fixing two behavioral changes:

1. The sliceToMapHook now handles map[string]interface{} in addition to
   map[interface{}]interface{}, as newer YAML parsing returns the former.

2. Viper v1.21+ added insensitiveArray() which recursively lowercases
   keys inside arrays, breaking the array-based workaround for
   case-sensitive map keys. Added restoreCaseSensitiveArrayKeys() to
   re-read config files directly and restore original key casing within
   arrays.

Relates to https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/issues/5469

fix: render msgpack IO with non-string map keys instead of base64

A task returning e.g. `dict[int, int]` ships as a msgpack Binary scalar under
a STRUCT type, since a LiteralMap can only hold string keys. Two things went
wrong when the console asked the translator to render one:

- `msgpack.Unmarshal` into `any` decodes maps as `map[string]any` and so fails
  with `invalid code=3 decoding string/bytes length` on the first int key,
  falling back to an unreadable base64 blob (`o0: hQNuBGMBcwVRAl8=`).
- A STRUCT with no metadata (which is what the SDK emits for such a dict — it
  has no dataclass schema to attach) hard-errored in `literalTypeToJsonSchema`,
  failing the whole conversion.

Decode maps untyped and stringify the keys, since JSON objects only have
string keys, and fall back to an open object schema when a STRUCT carries no
metadata. The same output now renders as
`{"1": 115, "2": 95, "3": 110, "4": 99, "5": 81}`.

build(deps): bump go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlpmetric/otlpmetrichttp (#7856)

fix: tell Spark which template container to adopt

Renaming the container makes the operator's webhook deterministic but not
Spark's own selection: with
spark.kubernetes.{driver,executor}.podTemplateContainerName unset, Spark
adopts the first container in the template and treats the rest as
sidecars. A pod template that orders a sidecar ahead of the task
container therefore has Spark run the sidecar as the driver.

Set both keys to the container this plugin renames. Left unset for a
custom driver/executor pod spec, whose primary container the plugin does
not choose -- that keeps Spark's existing first-container default rather
than pointing it at a name that may not be there.

runs: accept a "search" ListRuns filter matching run name or task name

The console's Runs page search box sends a single `task_name CONTAINS`
filter, so searching by run ID never worked. The Filter proto has no OR and
ListRuns ANDs every filter, so the console cannot express "run name OR task
name" on its own.

Add a synthetic "search" filter field, resolved by the run service before
the generic column allow-list conversion sees the request:

  search CONTAINS_CASE_INSENSITIVE x -> (LOWER(run_name) LIKE LOWER('%x%')) OR (LOWER(task_name) LIKE LOWER('%x%'))
  search CONTAINS x                  -> (run_name LIKE '%x%') OR (task_name LIKE '%x%')
  search EQUAL x                     -> (run_name = x) OR (task_name = x)

Any other function, or a missing, empty or multi-value term, is an
InvalidArgument. No IDL change: Filter.field is a free-form string validated
server-side. The Union cloud run service accepts the same field, so one
console request works against both backends; the console change follows
separately and must ship after this.

WatchGroups is left alone: the OSS grouped view does not consume request
filters at all.

fix(spark): pass driver/executor pod specs through as the pod template

The custom driver/executor pod spec was merged onto the pod spec Flyte
builds. That merge matches containers by name, and the container Flyte
generates is named after the task execution ID, so any container the user
named something else (the operator's own spark-kubernetes-{driver,executor},
or "primary") was silently dropped. Setting primary_container_name to such a
container failed the task outright with "invalid TaskSpecification, container
[...] not defined".

Hand the pod spec to the spark operator verbatim as spec.{driver,executor}
.template instead, and drop the primary_container_name override. The operator
patches the template onto the container it generates, which is the container
users are actually naming.

fix: apply Ray group extended resources once via ToK8sPodSpec

Addresses review feedback: applying group-level extended resources on top
of a base pod spec that already had task-level extended resources applied
could produce conflicting required node-affinity requirements (the same
GPU label ANDed with two different values, making the pod unschedulable)
or duplicate shared-memory volume/mount errors.

Instead, each group's pod spec is now built by layering the group's
extended_resources into the task overrides (group overrides execution-level
overrides, which override task-level defaults) and rebuilding the pod spec
once via ToK8sPodSpec, which computes the effective merge. Groups without
their own extended_resources reuse the already-built base pod spec.

This reverts the earlier flytek8s.ApplyExtendedResources extraction (no
longer needed). Adds a test covering task-level + group-level override.

Bind app inputs to a pinned artifact version, and list apps by consumed artifact

App inputs could reference an artifact two ways: `artifact_query`, resolved
server-side at some unspecified time, and `artifact_id`, an `ArtifactID` whose
version was optional.

Both were the wrong shape for what apps need. An app input has to name one
exact artifact version: the client resolves the artifact at deploy time and the
app runs against that version until it is redeployed. A query that the server
re-resolves later, or an ID with the version left off, both describe a moving
reference the app can silently drift across.

Replace them with a single `artifact_id` of type `ArtifactVersionId`, which
carries the version as a required part of its identity. The field is recorded
for lineage: the server does not resolve or validate it.

Both fields were declared in #7715 and never implemented -- no server ever read
them and no client ever set them -- so they are removed outright rather than
reserved. The new field takes 6 rather than reusing 3 or 4, so the numbers that
did ship are not given a new meaning.

Also add `ConsumedArtifactFilter` to app `ListRequest`, so callers can ask which
apps consume a given artifact -- the reverse of the lineage the pinned id
records. An empty version matches any version.

[BUG] use deep copy of bit arrays when getting array node state (#5681)

* [BUG] add retries to handle array node eventing race condition (#421)

If there is an error updating a [FlyteWorkflow CRD](https://github.com/unionai/flyte/blob/6a7207c5345604a28a9d4e3699becff767f520f5/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/handler.go#L378), then the propeller streak ends without the CRD getting updated and the in-memory copy of the FlyteWorkflow is not utilized on the next loop.

[TaskPhaseVersion](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/apis/flyteworkflow/v1alpha1/node_status.go#L239) is stored in the FlyteWorkflow. This is incremented when there is an update to node/subnode state to ensure that events are unique. If the events stay in the same state and have the same TaskPhaseVersion, then they [get short-circuited and don't get emitted to admin](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/events/admin_eventsink.go#L59) or will get returned as an [AlreadyExists error](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flyteadmin/pkg/manager/impl/task_execution_manager.go#L172) and get [handled in propeller to not bubble up in an error](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/nodes/node_exec_context.go#L38).

We can run into issues with ArrayNode eventing when:
- array node handler increments task phase version from "0" to "1"
- admin event sink emits event with version "1"
- the propeller controller is not able to update the FlyteWorkflow CRD, so the ArrayNodeStatus indicates taskPhaseVersion is still 0
- next loop, array node handler increments task phase version from "0" to "1"
- admin event sink prevents the event from getting emitted as an event with the same ID has already been received. No error is bubbled up.

This means we lose subnode state until there is an event that contains an update to that subnode. If the lost state is the subnode reaching a terminal state, then the subnode state (from admin/UI) is "stuck" in a non-terminal state.

I confirmed this to be an issue in the load-test-cluster. Whenever, there was an [error syncing the FlyteWorkflow](https://github.com/flyteorg/flyte/blob/37b4e13ac4a3594ac63b7a35058f4b2220e51282/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/workers.go#L91), the next round of eventing in ArrayNode would fail unless the ArrayNode phase changed.

feat(executor): add OTel metrics for the TaskAction controller

Build on the meter provider from #7459 to instrument the TaskAction controller
with two metrics the framework doesn't provide:

- taskaction.active (Int64ObservableGauge): number of TaskAction CRDs by plugin
  phase, observed asynchronously by listing from the controller cache.
- taskaction.crd.size_bytes (Int64Histogram): serialized size of a TaskAction
  CRD, recorded per reconcile.

Both are emitted via otelutils.GetMeterProvider("executor"), so they flow
through the same OTLP pipeline as the RPC metrics. Registration is non-fatal
(degrades to no custom metrics) and observeCRDSize is nil-safe.

Reconcile rate/latency, workqueue depth, and k8s API r/w latency are already
exposed by the controller-runtime metrics server; event-proxy send latency is
already captured by the otelconnect-wrapped events client.

feat(devbox): optional Grafana/Prometheus/OTel stack

    make devbox-run           # unchanged, still 1.7 GB
    make devbox-monitoring    # adds the stack
    make devbox-monitoring-stop

Reading the RPC metrics from a devbox meant standing up a collector,
Prometheus and Grafana by hand, and porting the Flyte v2 dashboard along with
them. This bundles that as one target.

It is opt-in rather than baked into the image on purpose. Preloading the three
images was measured at +1.43 GB unpacked (Grafana 704 MB, Prometheus 404 MB,
collector 334 MB), taking the devbox from 1.7 GB to 3.13 GB — 84% larger for
something most devbox users never open. Pulled on demand instead, the default
image is untouched and the images arrive in ~20s.

No operator and no CRDs: a static scrape config is enough for one node. Two
collector settings are load-bearing and easy to lose when editing:

  - max_recv_msg_size_mib: 64 — otelconnect's cumulative payload exceeds the
    4 MiB default and exports fail with ResourceExhausted.
  - resource_to_telemetry_conversion — without it service.name never becomes a
    label, the dashboard's `service` variable is empty, and every per-service
    panel has nothing to group by. This one only shows up as an empty dropdown,
    so it reads as "the dashboard is broken" rather than "the config is wrong".

`start` also publishes 30300 so the Grafana NodePort is reachable; a devbox
created before this change needs recreating for the URL to work, which
`make devbox-monitoring` now detects and says rather than printing a dead link.

fix: declare spec.sparkVersion on SparkApplications that carry a pod template

The kubeflow operator's validating webhook denies any SparkApplication
that sets a driver or executor pod template while declaring a Spark
version below 3.0.0:

  admission webhook "validate-sparkoperator-k8s-io-v1beta2-sparkapplication...
  denied the request: pod template feature requires Spark version 3.0.0 or higher

The plugin never set spec.sparkVersion, and an unset value loses that
comparison -- CompareSemanticVersion prefixes with "v" and hands "v" to
semver.Compare, where an invalid version sorts below every valid one. So
every spark task fails admission on a v2 operator once pod templates are
enabled, regardless of what Spark the image actually ships.

Declare the version, from a new plugins.spark.spark-version config, only
when a template is attached -- the single case the operator reads it for.
The default is the 3.0.0 floor the feature requires rather than a guess
at the image contents: the operator compares only against that boundary,
and declaring >= 3.0.0 is what tells it to let spark-submit apply the
template instead of mutating the pod itself.

fix(actions): coalesce TaskAction watch events by key + record true action start

Under high concurrency the actions-client processed every informer event
synchronously (per-event run-service RPC + k8s label patch) and stamped
created_at at record time, so backlogged events collapsed action duration
toward zero and inflated the multi-workflow concurrency runtime.

Coalescing: dispatchEvent now dedupes updates by TaskAction name (global
pending set); the worker clears the marker and reads the latest object from
the shared cache instead of a stale queued snapshot, so a queued->running->
succeeded burst that piles up while workers are behind collapses to a single
terminal notification. Deletes bypass coalescing (they carry the tombstone).
RecordAction now fires on first-seen (bloom-deduped) rather than only on Added,
since a coalesced first event may arrive as Modified.

Duration: the client sends the CRD creationTimestamp as ActionStatus.start_time;
the run service threads it into UpdateActionPhase, which corrects created_at via
LEAST(created_at, start) so duration reflects real wall-clock even when recorded
late. Uses the existing start_time field, no proto change.

Also bumps WatchWorkers 10->100 and WatchBufferSize 100->1000.

Tests: coalescing dedupe + latest-state read; duration correction (start time
drives duration, nil falls back to created_at).

[Bug] Update resource failures w/ Finalizers set  (#423)

## Overview
when [informer cache has stale values](https://github.com/unionai/flyte/blob/1e82352dd95f89630e333fe6105d5fdb5487a24e/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/nodes/task/k8s/plugin_manager.go#L478), we cannot update the k8s resource when [clearing finalizers](https://github.com/unionai/flyte/blob/1e82352dd95f89630e333fe6105d5fdb5487a24e/flytepropeller/pkg/controller/nodes/task/k8s/plugin_manager.go#L450) and get `Error: Operation cannot be fulfilled on pods.` The current implementation bubbles up the error resulting in a system retry. By the next loop, the informer cache is up to date and the update is able to be applied. However, in an ArrayNode with many subnodes getting executed in parallel, the execution can easily run out of retries.

This update adds a basic retry with exponential backoff to wait for the informer cache to get up to date.

## Test Plan
Ran in dogfood-gcp
- https://buildkite.com/unionai/managed-cluster-staging-sync/builds/4622 + manually updated configmap to enabled finalizers
- Run without change (https://dogfood-gcp.cloud-staging.union.ai/console/projects/flytesnacks/domains/development/executions/fd16ac81fd7b5480fb6f/nodes)
- Run with change (https://dogfood-gcp.cloud-staging.union.ai/console/projects/flytesnacks/domains/development/executions/f016a3be7fa304db5a77/nodeId/n0/nodes)
confirmed in logs that conflict errors:
```
{"json":{"exec_id":"f016a3be7fa304db5a77","node":"n0/n42","ns":"development","res_ver":"146129599","routine":"worker-66","src":"plugin_manager.go:455","wf":"flytesnacks:development:tests.flytekit.integration.map_task_issue.wf8"},"level":"warning","msg":"Failed to clear finalizers for Resource with name: development/f016a3be7fa304db5a77-n0-0-n42-0. Error: Operation cannot be fulfilled on pods \"f016a3be7fa304db5a77-n0-0-n42-0\": the object has been modified; please apply your changes to the latest version and try again","ts":"2024-08-17T02:02:48Z"}

```
did not bubble up + confirmed finalizers were removed:

```
➜  ~ k get pods -n development f016a3be7fa304db5a77-n0-0-n42-0 -o json | grep -i final
INFO[0000] [0] Couldn't find a config file []. Relying on env vars and pflags.
```
